This module enforces no ordering itself (the storage layer does); points\n//! are encoded in the order given.\n\nuse crate::bitio::{BitReader, BitWriter, ReadError};\n\n/// One timestamped integer sample.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Point {\n    pub ts: i64,\n    pub value: i64,\n}\n\nimpl Point {\n    pub fn new(ts: i64, value: i64) -> Self {\n        Self { ts, value }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Map a signed integer to an unsigned one preserving magnitude ordering\n/// (small absolute values become small unsigned values).\n/// Computed in i128 so that extreme inputs such as i64::MIN cannot overflow.\npub fn zigzag_encode(v: i64) -> u64 {\n    (((v as i128) << 1) ^ ((v as i128) >> 63)) as u64\n}\n\npub fn zigzag_decode(v: u64) -> i64 {\n    ((v >> 1) as i64) ^ -((v & 1) as i64)\n}\n\n/// Encode a block of points into the on-disk payload bytes\n/// (4-byte little-endian count followed by the bit stream).\npub fn encode_block(points: &[Point]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(4 + points.len() * 2);\n    out.extend_from_slice(&(points.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n\n    let mut w = BitWriter::with_capacity(points.len() * 2);\n    if let Some(first) = points.first() {\n        w.write_u64(first.ts as u64);\n        w.write_u64(first.value as u64);\n\n        // Timestamp predictor. The running delta is i128 because a DOD may\n        // be small even when the raw delta exceeds i64.\n        let mut prev_ts: i64 = first.ts;\n        let mut prev_delta: Option<i128> = None;\n        // Value predictor.\n        let mut prev_value: i64 = first.value;\n\n        for p in &points[1..] {\n            // ---- timestamp ----\n            let cur_delta = (p.ts as i128) - (prev_ts as i128);\n            match prev_delta {\n                Some(delta) => {\n                    let dod = cur_delta - delta;\n                    match i64::try_from(dod) {\n                        Ok(dod64) => {\n                            w.write_bit(false); // tag 0: delta-of-delta\n                            w.write_varint_u64(zigzag_encode(dod64));\n                            prev_delta = Some(cur_delta);\n                        }\n                        Err(_) => {\n                            w.write_bit(true); // tag 1: raw escape\n                            w.write_u64(p.ts as u64);\n                            prev_delta = None;\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                None => {\n                    // First point after a reset: store a fresh raw delta.\n                    match i64::try_from(cur_delta) {\n                        Ok(d) => {\n                            w.write_bit(false); // tag 0: initial delta\n                            w.write_varint_u64(zigzag_encode(d));\n                            prev_delta = Some(cur_delta);\n                        }\n                        Err(_) => {\n                            w.write_bit(true); // tag 1: raw escape\n                            w.write_u64(p.ts as u64);\n                            // Stay reset: even the single delta overflows.\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            prev_ts = p.ts;\n\n            // ---- value ----\n            let diff = (p.value as i128) - (prev_value as i128);\n            match i64::try_from(diff) {\n                Ok(d) => {\n                    w.write_bit(false);\n                    w.write_varint_u64(zigzag_encode(d));\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    w.write_bit(true);\n                    w.write_u64(p.value as u64);\n                }\n            }\n            prev_value = p.value;\n        }\n    }\n    out.extend_from_slice(&w.finish());\n    out\n}\n\n/// Decode a block payload produced by [`encode_block`].\npub fn decode_block(payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Point>, CodecError> {\n    if payload.len() < 4 {\n        return Err(CodecError::Truncated);\n    }\n    let count = u32::from_le_bytes([payload[0], payload[1], payload[2], payload[3]]) as usize;\n    let mut r = BitReader::new(&payload[4..]);\n    if count == 0 {\n        return Ok(Vec::new());\n    }\n\n    let first_ts = r.read_u64()? as i64;\n    let first_value = r.read_u64()? as i64;\n    let mut points = Vec::with_capacity(count);\n    points.push(Point::new(first_ts, first_value));\n\n    let mut prev_ts = first_ts;\n    let mut prev_delta: Option<i128> = None;\n    let mut prev_value = first_value;\n\n    for _ in 1..count {\n        // ---- timestamp ----\n        let ts = if !r.read_bit()? {\n            let d_signed = zigzag_decode(r.read_varint_u64()?) as i128;\n            let cur_delta = match prev_delta {\n                Some(delta) => delta + d_signed, // delta-of-delta\n                None => d_signed,                // initial delta after reset\n            };\n            let ts = (prev_ts as i128) + cur_delta;\n            prev_delta = Some(cur_delta);\n            i64::try_from(ts).map_err(|_| CodecError::Overflow)?\n        } else {\n            let raw = r.read_u64()? as i64;\n            prev_delta = None;\n            raw\n        };\n        prev_ts = ts;\n\n        // ---- value ----\n        let value = if !r.read_bit()? {\n            let d = zigzag_decode(r.read_varint_u64()?) as i128;\n            let v = (prev_value as i128) + d;\n            i64::try_from(v).map_err(|_| CodecError::Overflow)?\n        } else {\n            r.read_u64()? as i64\n        };\n        prev_value = value;\n\n        points.push(Point::new(ts, value));\n    }\n\n    Ok(points)\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CodecError {\n    Truncated,\n    UnexpectedEof,\n    /// A reconstructed value did not fit in `i64` (corrupt stream).\n    Overflow,\n}\n\nimpl From<ReadError> for CodecError {\n    fn from(_: ReadError) -> Self {\n        CodecError::UnexpectedEof\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for CodecError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            CodecError::Truncated => write!(f, \"block payload truncated\"),\n            CodecError::UnexpectedEof => write!(f, \"unexpected end of block bit stream\"),\n            CodecError::Overflow => write!(f, \"reconstructed integer overflows i64\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for CodecError {}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn roundtrip(points: {"parentUuid":"d63e44f2-22ed-41e0-b84f-843addc43113","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_undi5hn4fkrbmt6sild1crob","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp7/b/src/crc.rs","content":"//! CRC-32/ISO-HDLC (the zlib/gzip polynomial, reflected, init 0xFFFF_FFFF,\n//! final XOR 0xFFFF_FFFF). Used to frame on-disk records so a torn write or\n//! corrupted tail can be detected and truncated on open.\n\n/// Precomputed table for the reflected polynomial 0xEDB8_8320.\nconst fn make_table() -> [u32; 256] {\n    let mut table = [0u32; 256];\n    let mut i = 0usize;\n    while i < 256 {\n        let mut c = i as u32;\n        let mut j = 0;\n        while j < 8 {\n            c = if c & 1 != 0 {\n                0xEDB8_8320 ^ (c >> 1)\n            } else {\n                c >> 1\n            };\n            j += 1;\n        }\n        table[i] = c;\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    table\n}\n\nconst TABLE: [u32; 256] = make_table();\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct Crc32 {\n    state: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Crc32 {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self { state: 0xFFFF_FFFF }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Crc32 {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    pub fn update(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {\n        let mut c = self.state;\n        for &b in bytes {\n            c = TABLE[((c ^ b as u32) & 0xff) as usize] ^ (c >> 8);\n        }\n        self.state = c;\n    }\n\n    pub fn finish(self) -> u32 {\n        self.state ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n    }\n\n    /// One-shot checksum.\n    pub fn checksum(bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n        let mut c = Crc32::new();\n        c.update(bytes);\n        c.finish()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n {"parentUuid":"41a5c0f2-5490-49cb-8c79-ab8a8678c084","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_suq21axxmkbs10y8yz95lgmr","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp7/b/src/io_layer.rs","content":"//! Injectable storage I/O layer.\n//!\n//! The storage engine never touches `std::fs` directly. It talks to the two\n//! traits below, so tests can deterministically inject the two failure modes\n//! that matter for durability:\n//!\n//! * **partial/failed writes** (simulated `ENOSPC`): a write past a configured\n//!   byte budget performs the partial write that fits and then fails, leaving\n//!   a torn record on disk;\n//! * **failed `fsync`** (simulated power-loss / barrier failure): the data may\n//!   be in the page cache but was not made durable.\n//!\n//! All I/O is positional (`*_at`), so there is no shared cursor per file and\n//! no seek state to corrupt. The production backend ([`RealIo`]) implements\n//! the traits with `std::fs` and the Unix `FileExt` pread/pwrite equivalents.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, AtomicUsize, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// A single open file supporting positional reads/writes and durability calls.\npub trait IoFile: Send {\n    /// Write all of `buf` at absolute byte `offset`.\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Positional read; returns the number of bytes read (0 at EOF).\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize>;\n    /// Flush file data and metadata to stable storage (`fsync`).\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Truncate or extend the file to exactly `len` bytes.\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Current file length in bytes.\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64>;\n}\n\n/// Opens files and performs namespace operations inside one data directory.\npub trait IoBackend: Send + Sync {\n    /// Exclusive create; fails if the path already exists.\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// Open an existing file for read + write.\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// Open an existing file read-only.\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// `fsync` a directory (required to persist a rename/create).\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Atomically rename `from` to `to` within the filesystem.\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Read an entire small file (used for the series metadata file).\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Production backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]\npub struct RealIo;\n\nimpl RealIo {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        RealIo\n    }\n}\n\nstruct RealFile {\n    f: fs::File,\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nmod unix_ext {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;\n\n    impl IoFile for RealFile {\n        fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n            self.f.write_all_at(buf, offset)\n        }\n        fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize> {\n            self.f.read_at(buf, offset)\n        }\n        fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n            self.f.sync_all()\n        }\n        fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n            self.f.set_len(len)\n        }\n        fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64> {\n            Ok(self.f.metadata()?.len())\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IoBackend for RealIo {\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .create_new(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::OpenOptions::new().read(true).write(true).open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::File::open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let f = fs::File::open(path)?;\n        f.sync_all()\n    }\n\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        fs::rename(from, to)\n    }\n\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        fs::read(path)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Fault-injecting backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Raw OS error numbers used so injected failures look like real I/O errors.\n/// `ENOSPC` = 28, `EIO` = 5 on Linux.\npub const ENOSPC: i32 = 28;\npub const EIO: i32 = 5;\n\n/// Mutable fault configuration shared by every file handed out by a\n/// [`FaultyIo`] backend. Reconfigure through an `Arc<FaultRules>` at runtime\n/// (that is what the `/dev/fault` HTTP endpoint does).\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct FaultRules {\n    /// Once this many total bytes have been written across all files,\n    /// further writes return `ENOSPC`. A write straddling the boundary\n    /// performs the fitting prefix first (a genuine torn write).\n    pub fail_write_total: Option<u64>,\n    /// The next N `sync` calls return `EIO` (then syncs succeed again).\n    fail_sync_remaining: AtomicUsize,\n    bytes_written: AtomicU64,\n}\n\nimpl Default for FaultRules {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            fail_write_total: None,\n            fail_sync_remaining: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n            bytes_written: AtomicU64::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FaultRules {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Make the next `n` sync calls fail with EIO.\n    pub fn fail_next_syncs(&self, n: usize) {\n        self.fail_sync_remaining.store(n, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    /// Cap total successful/partial write bytes at `limit`.\n    pub fn fail_writes_after(&self, limit: u64) {\n        self.fail_write_total = Some(limit); // interior mutability via &self below\n    }\n\n    /// Remove all injected faults and reset counters.\n    pub fn clear(&self) {\n        // Interior mutability: the fields are atomics; `fail_write_total` is\n        // accessed only here, and callers only hold `Arc<FaultRules>`. We\n        // therefore keep the byte limit in an atomic too.\n        self.fail_sync_remaining.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        self.bytes_written.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        self.write_limit.store(u64::MAX, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    pub fn bytes_written(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n}\n\n// Internal storage for the write limit so `clear` can take `&self`.\nimpl FaultRules {\n    // See the constructor: these extra atomics are declared on the struct\n    // below through a wrapper; kept here as documentation of intent.\n}\n\n/// Backend that delegates to `inner` but injects failures per `rules`.\npub struct FaultyIo {\n    inner: Arc<dyn IoBackend>,\n    rules: Arc<FaultRules>,\n}\n\nimpl FaultyIo {\n    pub fn new(inner: Arc<dyn IoBackend>, rules: Arc<FaultRules>) -> Self {\n        Self { inner, rules }\n    }\n\n    pub fn rules(&self) -> Arc<FaultRules> {\n        Arc::clone(&self.rules)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct FaultyFile {\n    inner: Box<dyn IoFile>,\n    rules: Arc<FaultRules>,\n}\n\nimpl IoFile for FaultyFile {\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let limit = self.rules.write_limit.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let used = self.rules.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let budget = limit.saturating_sub(used);\n        let end = offset.saturating_add(buf.len() as u64);\n        if (end <= offset) || (buf.len() as u64 > budget && offset.wrapping_add(0) >= used.wrapping_add(budget.min(u64::MAX)))\n        {\n            // Unreachable in normal use; fall through to the boundary logic.\n        }\n        if (buf.len() as u64) <= budget {\n            self.inner.write_all_at(buf, offset)?;\n            self.rules\n                .bytes_written\n                .fetch_add(buf.len() as u64, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        // Straddles or starts past the budget: perform the partial prefix.\n        let fit = budget as usize;\n        if fit > 0 {\n            self.inner.write_all_at(&buf[..fit], offset)?;\n            self.rules\n                .bytes_written\n                .fetch_add(fit as u64, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        }\n        Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(ENOSPC))\n    }\n\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize> {\n        self.inner.read_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut remaining = self.rules.fail_sync_remaining.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        if remaining > 0 {\n            // Decrement exactly once even under concurrency.\n            while remaining > 0 {\n                match self.rules.fail_sync_remaining.compare_exchange(\n                    remaining,\n                    remaining - 1,\n                    Ordering::SeqCst,\n                    Ordering::SeqCst,\n                ) {\n                    Ok(_) => return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(EIO)),\n                    Err(v) => remaining = v,\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.set_len(len)\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64> {\n        self.inner.len()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IoBackend for FaultyIo {\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        Ok(Box::new(FaultyFile {\n            inner: self.inner.create_new(path)?,\n            rules: Arc::clone(&self.rules),\n        }))\n    }\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        Ok(Box::new(FaultyFile {\n            inner: self.inner.open_write(path)?,\n            rules: Arc::clone(&self.rules),\n        }))\n    }\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        self.inner.open_read(path)\n    }\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.sync_dir(path)\n    }\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.rename(from, to)\n    }\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.inner.read_exact_file(path)\n    }\n}\n\n// Helper so callers can build data paths without importing PathBuf types.\npub fn join(dir: &Path, name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    dir.join(name)\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_e996a663e9c4b42d4df20380","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1339,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":47928,"output_tokens":4457,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_suq21axxmkbs10y8yz95lgmr":{"content":"//! Injectable storage I/O layer.\n//!\n//! The storage engine never touches `std::fs` directly. It talks to the two\n//! traits below, so tests can deterministically inject the two failure modes\n//! that matter for durability:\n//!\n//! * **partial/failed writes** (simulated `ENOSPC`): after a configured total\n//!   number of bytes has been written, the tail of a straddling write is\n//!   rejected with `ENOSPC` while its fitting prefix is persisted, leaving a\n//!   torn record on disk;\n//! * **failed `fsync`** (simulated barrier / power failure): the next N sync\n//!   calls return `EIO`.\n//!\n//! All file I/O is positional (`*_at`), so there is no shared cursor per file\n//! and no seek state to corrupt. The production backend ([`RealIo`])\n//! implements the traits with `std::fs` and the Unix `FileExt` pread/pwrite\n//! equivalents.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, AtomicUsize, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// A single open file supporting positional reads/writes and durability calls.\npub trait IoFile: Send {\n    /// Write all of `buf` at absolute byte `offset`.\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Positional read; returns the number of bytes read (0 at EOF).\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize>;\n    /// Flush file data and metadata to stable storage (`fsync`).\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Truncate or extend the file to exactly `len` bytes.\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Current file length in bytes.\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64>;\n}\n\n/// Opens files and performs namespace operations inside one data directory.\npub trait IoBackend: Send + Sync {\n    /// Exclusive create; fails if the path already exists.\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// Open an existing file for read + write.\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// Open an existing file read-only.\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// `fsync` a directory (required to persist a rename/create).\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Atomically rename `from` to `to` within the filesystem.\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Read an entire small file.\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Production backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]\npub struct RealIo;\n\nimpl RealIo {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        RealIo\n    }\n}\n\nstruct RealFile {\n    f: fs::File,\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nuse std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nimpl IoFile for RealFile {\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.f.write_all_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize> {\n        self.f.read_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.f.sync_all()\n    }\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.f.set_len(len)\n    }\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64> {\n        Ok(self.f.metadata()?.len())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IoBackend for RealIo {\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .create_new(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::File::open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        fs::File::open(path)?.sync_all()\n    }\n\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        fs::rename(from, to)\n    }\n\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        fs::read(path)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Fault-injecting backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Raw Linux error numbers so injected failures are indistinguishable from\n/// real kernel errors: `ENOSPC` = 28, `EIO` = 5.\npub const ENOSPC: i32 = 28;\npub const EIO: i32 = 5;\n\n/// Mutable fault configuration shared by every file handed out by a\n/// [`FaultyIo`] backend. Reconfigure the shared `Arc<FaultRules>` at runtime;\n/// that is what the `/dev/fault` HTTP endpoint does.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct FaultRules {\n    /// Cumulative bytes that writes may cover before failing.\n    /// `u64::MAX` means \"no limit\".\n    write_limit: AtomicU64,\n    /// Bytes already charged against the limit.\n    bytes_written: AtomicU64,\n    /// Remaining `sync` calls that fail.\n    fail_sync_remaining: AtomicUsize,\n}\n\nimpl FaultRules {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            write_limit: AtomicU64::new(u64::MAX),\n            bytes_written: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            fail_sync_remaining: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// After `limit` more bytes have been written, writes fail with ENOSPC.\n    /// A write straddling the boundary persists its fitting prefix first.\n    pub fn fail_writes_after(&self, limit: u64) {\n        self.write_limit\n            .store(self.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst) + limit, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    /// The next `n` `sync` calls fail with EIO.\n    pub fn fail_next_syncs(&self, n: usize) {\n        self.fail_sync_remaining.store(n, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    /// Remove all injected faults (counters for already-spent bytes remain).\n    pub fn clear(&self) {\n        self.write_limit.store(u64::MAX, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        self.fail_sync_remaining.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    pub fn bytes_written(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Backend that delegates to `inner` but injects failures per `rules`.\npub struct FaultyIo {\n    inner: Arc<dyn IoBackend>,\n    rules: Arc<FaultRules>,\n}\n\nimpl FaultyIo {\n    pub fn new(inner: Arc<dyn IoBackend>, rules: Arc<FaultRules>) -> Self {\n        Self { inner, rules }\n    }\n\n    pub fn rules(&self) -> Arc<FaultRules> {\n        Arc::clone(&self.rules)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct FaultyFile {\n    inner: Box<dyn IoFile>,\n    rules: Arc<FaultRules>,\n}\n\nimpl IoFile for FaultyFile {\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let limit = self.rules.write_limit.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let used = self.rules.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let budget = limit.saturating_sub(used);\n        if (buf.len() as u64) <= budget {\n            self.inner.write_all_at(buf, offset)?;\n            self.rules\n                .bytes_written\n                .fetch_add(buf.len() as u64, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            // Persist the fitting prefix, charge it, then fail like ENOSPC.\n            let fit = budget as usize;\n            if fit > 0 {\n                self.inner.write_all_at(&buf[..fit], offset)?;\n                self.rules\n                    .bytes_written\n                    .fetch_add(fit as u64, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            }\n            Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(ENOSPC))\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize> {\n        self.inner.read_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut remaining = self.rules.fail_sync_remaining.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        while remaining > 0 {\n            match self.rules.fail_sync_remaining.compare_exchange(\n                remaining,\n                remaining - 1,\n                Ordering::SeqCst,\n                Ordering::SeqCst,\n            ) {\n                Ok(_) => return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(EIO)),\n                Err(v) => remaining = v,\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.set_len(len)\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64> -> io::Result<u64> {\n        self.inner.len()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IoBackend for FaultyIo {\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        Ok(Box::new(FaultyFile {\n            inner: self.inner.create_new(path)?,\n            rules: Arc::clone(&self.rules),\n        }))\n    }\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        Ok(Box::new(FaultyFile {\n            inner: self.inner.open_write(path)?,\n            rules: Arc::clone(&self.rules),\n        }))\n    }\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        self.inner.open_read(path)\n    }\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.sync_dir(path)\n    }\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.rename(from, to)\n    }\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.inner.read_exact_file(path)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a path inside `dir` (small helper for callers/tests).\npub fn join(dir: &Path, name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    dir.join(name)\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_16507ba4fd2cc7508e131608","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":3823,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":48952,"output_tokens":3056,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_9hvzt94w16helwagnj0hwstk":{"content":"//! Injectable storage I/O layer.\n//!\n//! The storage engine never touches `std::fs` directly. It talks to the two\n//! traits below, so tests can deterministically inject the two failure modes\n//! that matter for durability:\n//!\n//! * **partial/failed writes** (simulated `ENOSPC`): after a configured total\n//!   number of bytes has been written, the tail of a straddling write is\n//!   rejected with `ENOSPC` while its fitting prefix is persisted, leaving a\n//!   torn record on disk;\n//! * **failed `fsync`** (simulated barrier / power failure): the next N sync\n//!   calls return `EIO`.\n//!\n//! All file I/O is positional (`*_at`), so there is no shared cursor per file\n//! and no seek state to corrupt. The production backend ([`RealIo`])\n//! implements the traits with `std::fs` and the Unix `FileExt` pread/pwrite\n//! equivalents.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, AtomicUsize, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// A single open file supporting positional reads/writes and durability calls.\npub trait IoFile: Send {\n    /// Write all of `buf` at absolute byte `offset`.\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Positional read; returns the number of bytes read (0 at EOF).\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize>;\n    /// Flush file data and metadata to stable storage (`fsync`).\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Truncate or extend the file to exactly `len` bytes.\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Current file length in bytes.\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64>;\n}\n\n/// Opens files and performs namespace operations inside one data directory.\npub trait IoBackend: Send + Sync {\n    /// Exclusive create; fails if the path already exists.\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// Open an existing file for read + write.\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// Open an existing file read-only.\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// `fsync` a directory (required to persist a rename/create).\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Atomically rename `from` to `to` within the filesystem.\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Read an entire small file.\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Production backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]\npub struct RealIo;\n\nimpl RealIo {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        RealIo\n    }\n}\n\nstruct RealFile {\n    f: fs::File,\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nuse std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nimpl IoFile for RealFile {\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.f.write_all_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize> {\n        self.f.read_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.f.sync_all()\n    }\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.f.set_len(len)\n    }\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64> {\n        Ok(self.f.metadata()?.len())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IoBackend for RealIo {\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .create_new(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::File::open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        fs::File::open(path)?.sync_all()\n    }\n\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        fs::rename(from, to)\n    }\n\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        fs::read(path)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Fault-injecting backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Raw Linux error numbers so injected failures are indistinguishable from\n/// real kernel errors: `ENOSPC` = 28, `EIO` = 5.\npub const ENOSPC: i32 = 28;\npub const EIO: i32 = 5;\n\n/// Mutable fault configuration shared by every file handed out by a\n/// [`FaultyIo`] backend. Reconfigure the shared `Arc<FaultRules>` at runtime;\n/// that is what the `/dev/fault` HTTP endpoint does.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct FaultRules {\n    /// Cumulative bytes that writes may cover before failing.\n    /// `u64::MAX` means \"no limit\".\n    write_limit: AtomicU64,\n    /// Bytes already charged against the limit.\n    bytes_written: AtomicU64,\n    /// Remaining `sync` calls that fail.\n    fail_sync_remaining: AtomicUsize,\n}\n\nimpl FaultRules {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            write_limit: AtomicU64::new(u64::MAX),\n            bytes_written: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            fail_sync_remaining: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// After `limit` more bytes have been written, writes fail with ENOSPC.\n    /// A write straddling the boundary persists its fitting prefix first.\n    pub fn fail_writes_after(&self, limit: u64) {\n        self.write_limit\n            .store(self.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst) + limit, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    /// The next `n` `sync` calls fail with EIO.\n    pub fn fail_next_syncs(&self, n: usize) {\n        self.fail_sync_remaining.store(n, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    /// Remove all injected faults (counters for already-spent bytes remain).\n    pub fn clear(&self) {\n        self.write_limit.store(u64::MAX, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        self.fail_sync_remaining.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    pub fn bytes_written(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Backend that delegates to `inner` but injects failures per `rules`.\npub struct FaultyIo {\n    inner: Arc<dyn IoBackend>,\n    rules: Arc<FaultRules>,\n}\n\nimpl FaultyIo {\n    pub fn new(inner: Arc<dyn IoBackend>, rules: Arc<FaultRules>) -> Self {\n        Self { inner, rules }\n    }\n\n    pub fn rules(&self) -> Arc<FaultRules> {\n        Arc::clone(&self.rules)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct FaultyFile {\n    inner: Box<dyn IoFile>,\n    rules: Arc<FaultRules>,\n}\n\nimpl IoFile for FaultyFile {\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let limit = self.rules.write_limit.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let used = self.rules.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let budget = limit.saturating_sub(used);\n        if (buf.len() as u64) <= budget {\n            self.inner.write_all_at(buf, offset)?;\n            self.rules\n                .bytes_written\n                .fetch_add(buf.len() as u64, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            // Persist the fitting prefix, charge it, then fail like ENOSPC.\n            let fit = budget as usize;\n            if fit > 0 {\n                self.inner.write_all_at(&buf[..fit], offset)?;\n                self.rules\n                    .bytes_written\n                    .fetch_add(fit as u64, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            }\n            Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(ENOSPC))\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize> {\n        self.inner.read_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut remaining = self.rules.fail_sync_remaining.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        while remaining > 0 {\n            match self.rules.fail_sync_remaining.compare_exchange(\n                remaining,\n                remaining - 1,\n                Ordering::SeqCst,\n                Ordering::SeqCst,\n            ) {\n                Ok(_) => return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(EIO)),\n                Err(v) => remaining = v,\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.set_len(len)\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64> -> io::Result<u64> {\n        self.inner.len()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IoBackend for FaultyIo {\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        Ok(Box::new(FaultyFile {\n            inner: self.inner.create_new(path)?,\n            rules: Arc::clone(&self.rules),\n        }))\n    }\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        Ok(Box::new(FaultyFile {\n            inner: self.inner.open_write(path)?,\n            rules: Arc::clone(&self.rules),\n        }))\n    }\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        self.inner.open_read(path)\n    }\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.sync_dir(path)\n    }\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.rename(from, to)\n    }\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.inner.read_exact_file(path)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a path inside `dir` Injectable storage I/O layer.\n//!\n//! The storage engine never touches `std::fs` directly. It talks to the two\n//! traits below, so tests can deterministically inject the two failure modes\n//! that matter for durability:\n//!\n//! * **partial/failed writes** (simulated `ENOSPC`): after a configured total\n//!   number of bytes has been written, the tail of a straddling write is\n//!   rejected with `ENOSPC` while its fitting prefix is persisted, leaving a\n//!   torn record on disk;\n//! * **failed `fsync`** (simulated barrier / power failure): the next N sync\n//!   calls return `EIO`.\n//!\n//! All file I/O is positional (`*_at`), so there is no shared cursor per file\n//! and no seek state to corrupt. The production backend ([`RealIo`])\n//! implements the traits with `std::fs` and the Unix `FileExt` pread/pwrite\n//! equivalents.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, AtomicUsize, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// A single open file supporting positional reads/writes and durability calls.\npub trait IoFile: Send {\n    /// Write all of `buf` at absolute byte `offset`.\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Positional read; returns the number of bytes read (0 at EOF).\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize>;\n    /// Flush file data and metadata to stable storage (`fsync`).\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Truncate or extend the file to exactly `len` bytes.\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Current file length in bytes.\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64>;\n}\n\n/// Opens files and performs namespace operations inside one data directory.\npub trait IoBackend: Send + Sync {\n    /// Exclusive create; fails if the path already exists.\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// Open an existing file for read + write.\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// Open an existing file read-only.\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>>;\n    /// `fsync` a directory (required to persist a rename/create).\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Atomically rename `from` to `to` within the filesystem.\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n    /// Read an entire small file.\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Production backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]\npub struct RealIo;\n\nimpl RealIo {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        RealIo\n    }\n}\n\nstruct RealFile {\n    f: fs::File,\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nuse std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nimpl IoFile for RealFile {\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.f.write_all_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize> {\n        self.f.read_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.f.sync_all()\n    }\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.f.set_len(len)\n    }\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64> {\n        Ok(self.f.metadata()?.len())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IoBackend for RealIo {\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .create_new(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        let f = fs::File::open(path)?;\n        Ok(Box::new(RealFile { f }))\n    }\n\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        fs::File::open(path)?.sync_all()\n    }\n\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        fs::rename(from, to)\n    }\n\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        fs::read(path)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Fault-injecting backend\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Raw Linux error numbers so injected failures are indistinguishable from\n/// real kernel errors: `ENOSPC` = 28, `EIO` = 5.\npub const ENOSPC: i32 = 28;\npub const EIO: i32 = 5;\n\n/// Mutable fault configuration shared by every file handed out by a\n/// [`FaultyIo`] backend. Reconfigure the shared `Arc<FaultRules>` at runtime;\n/// that is what the `/dev/fault` HTTP endpoint does.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct FaultRules {\n    /// Cumulative bytes that writes may cover before failing.\n    /// `u64::MAX` means \"no limit\".\n    write_limit: AtomicU64,\n    /// Bytes already charged against the limit.\n    bytes_written: AtomicU64,\n    /// Remaining `sync` calls that fail.\n    fail_sync_remaining: AtomicUsize,\n}\n\nimpl FaultRules {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            write_limit: AtomicU64::new(u64::MAX),\n            bytes_written: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            fail_sync_remaining: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// After `limit` more bytes have been written, writes fail with ENOSPC.\n    /// A write straddling the boundary persists its fitting prefix first.\n    pub fn fail_writes_after(&self, limit: u64) {\n        self.write_limit\n            .store(self.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst) + limit, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    /// The next `n` `sync` calls fail with EIO.\n    pub fn fail_next_syncs(&self, n: usize) {\n        self.fail_sync_remaining.store(n, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    /// Remove all injected faults (counters for already-spent bytes remain).\n    pub fn clear(&self) {\n        self.write_limit.store(u64::MAX, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        self.fail_sync_remaining.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    pub fn bytes_written(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Backend that delegates to `inner` but injects failures per `rules`.\npub struct FaultyIo {\n    inner: Arc<dyn IoBackend>,\n    rules: Arc<FaultRules>,\n}\n\nimpl FaultyIo {\n    pub fn new(inner: Arc<dyn IoBackend>, rules: Arc<FaultRules>) -> Self {\n        Self { inner, rules }\n    }\n\n    pub fn rules(&self) -> Arc<FaultRules> {\n        Arc::clone(&self.rules)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct FaultyFile {\n    inner: Box<dyn IoFile>,\n    rules: Arc<FaultRules>,\n}\n\nimpl IoFile for FaultyFile {\n    fn write_all_at(&mut self, buf: &[u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let limit = self.rules.write_limit.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let used = self.rules.bytes_written.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let budget = limit.saturating_sub(used);\n        if (buf.len() as u64) <= budget {\n            self.inner.write_all_at(buf, offset)?;\n            self.rules\n                .bytes_written\n                .fetch_add(buf.len() as u64, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            // Persist the fitting prefix, charge it, then fail like ENOSPC.\n            let fit = budget as usize;\n            if fit > 0 {\n                self.inner.write_all_at(&buf[..fit], offset)?;\n                self.rules\n                    .bytes_written\n                    .fetch_add(fit as u64, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            }\n            Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(ENOSPC))\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> io::Result<usize> {\n        self.inner.read_at(buf, offset)\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut remaining = self.rules.fail_sync_remaining.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        while remaining > 0 {\n            match self.rules.fail_sync_remaining.compare_exchange(\n                remaining,\n                remaining - 1,\n                Ordering::SeqCst,\n                Ordering::SeqCst,\n            ) {\n                Ok(_) => return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(EIO)),\n                Err(v) => remaining = v,\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n\n    fn set_len(&mut self, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.set_len(len)\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self) -> io::Result<u64> -> io::Result<u64> {\n        self.inner.len()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IoBackend for FaultyIo {\n    fn create_new(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        Ok(Box::new(FaultyFile {\n            inner: self.inner.create_new(path)?,\n            rules: Arc::clone(&self.rules),\n        }))\n    }\n    fn open_write(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        Ok(Box::new(FaultyFile {\n            inner: self.inner.open_write(path)?,\n            rules: Arc::clone(&self.rules),\n        }))\n    }\n    fn open_read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Box<dyn IoFile>> {\n        self.inner.open_read(path)\n    }\n    fn sync_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.sync_dir(path)\n    }\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.rename(from, to)\n    }\n    fn read_exact_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.inner.read_exact_file(path)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a path inside `dir` (small helper for callers/tests).\npub fn join(dir: &Path, name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    dir.join(name)\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":251,"oldLines":7,"newStart":251,"newLines":7,"lines":[" {"parentUuid":"d7d84109-0d2b-4643-8dd8-cc18c221e03d","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_7szpup19dtcbj4t3r8b1o82p","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp7/b/src/store.rs","content":"//! File-backed block storage engine.\n//!\n//! # On-disk format\n//!\n//! One series = one file `<data-dir>/<name>.tsb`:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! offset  size  field\n//! 0       4     magic  = b\"TSBK\"\n//! 4       2     version (u16 LE) = 1\n//! 6       2     flags (u16 LE); bit 0: unordered policy (0=reject, 1=buffer)\n//! 8       4     block_size (u32 LE)\n//! 12      8     reserved (8 zero bytes; future index pointer)\n//! 20      ...   records\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Each record:\n//! ```text\n//! payload_len : u32 LE\n//! crc32       : u32 LE   (CRC-32/ISO-HDLC over payload only)\n//! payload     : payload_len bytes, encoded by crate::coding\n//! ```\n//!\n//! The block index is **not** stored separately: on open the file is scanned\n//! record by record and an in-memory index (record offset, time range, count)\n//! is rebuilt. A torn trailing record (short header, length overrunning the\n//! file, or CRC mismatch — the signature of a crash or injected ENOSPC\n//! mid-write) ends the scan and is truncated away. This is the durability\n//! boundary:\n//!\n//! * a block is durable only after its record has been fully written **and**\n//!   `fsync`ed;\n//! * points still sitting in the in-memory active block are never durable;\n//! * a failed `fsync` is reported to the client as an error even though bytes\n//!   may be in the page cache — durability was not confirmed.\n//!\n//! # Ordering semantics\n//!\n//! A series is created with one of two policies for out-of-order points\n//! (`ts < last accepted ts`; equal timestamps are legal duplicates):\n//!\n//! * `Reject` (default): the whole write batch fails, nothing is accepted.\n//! * `Buffer`: late points go to a separate in-memory side buffer, are\n//!   excluded from every range query, and are only merged via an explicit\n//!   `drain`, which stable-sorts them by timestamp and inserts them through\n//!   the normal ordered path (which may reject them again if they are still\n//!   older than the newest accepted point).\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::coding::{self, Point};\nuse crate::crc::Crc32;\nuse crate::io_layer::IoBackend;\n\npub const MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b\"TSBK\";\npub const FORMAT_VERSION: u16 = 1;\npub const HEADER_LEN: u64 = 20;\n\nconst FLAG_BUFFER: u16 = 1;\n\n/// What happens to points whose timestamp is older than the newest point\n/// already accepted by the series.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum UnorderedPolicy {\n    /// Reject the whole batch with [`StoreError::OutOfOrder`].\n    Reject,\n    /// Park late points in a side buffer; merge later with an explicit drain.\n    Buffer,\n}\n\n/// Index entry for one flushed block.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct BlockMeta {\n    /// Absolute offset of the record header (the length field).\n    pub record_offset: u64,\n    pub payload_len: u32,\n    pub first_ts: i64,\n    pub last_ts: i64,\n    pub count: u32,\n}\n\n/// Result of opening a data directory.\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]\npub struct RecoverReport {\n    pub series_loaded: usize,\n    pub blocks_loaded: usize,\n    /// Number of trailing torn records truncated away.\n    pub torn_records: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StoreError {\n    Io(io::Error),\n    /// Directory is not a tsblock store (bad/absent magic).\n    NotAStore,\n    /// File header indicates a newer/unsupported format version.\n    UnsupportedVersion(u16),\n    /// Corruption detected away from the tail (CRC failure mid-file).\n    Corruption { series: String, detail: String },\n    SeriesExists(String),\n    UnknownSeries(String),\n    BadSeriesName(String),\n    /// At least one point was older than the series high-water mark.\n    /// Carries the offending timestamp.\n    OutOfOrder { ts: i64, last_ts: i64 },\n    /// Returned when `?policy=buffer` points remain after a failed drain.\n    DrainConflict { accepted: usize, rejected_ts: i64 },\n    Codec(String),\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for StoreError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StoreError::Io(e) => write!(f, {v}\"),\n            StoreError::Corruption { series, detail } => {\n                write!(f, \"corruption in series {series}: {detail}\")\n            }\n            StoreError::SeriesExists(s) => write!(f, \"series {s:?} already exists\"),\n            StoreError::UnknownSeries(s) => write!(f, \"unknown series {s:?}\"),\n            StoreError::BadSeriesName(s) => write!(f, \"bad series name {s:?}\"),\n            StoreError::OutOfOrder { ts, last_ts } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"out-of-order point ts={ts} is older than last accepted ts={last_ts}\"\n            ),\n at still-late ts={rejected_ts}\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::Codec(s) => write!(f, \"codec error: {s}\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StoreError {}\n\nimpl From<io::Error> for StoreError {\n    fn from(e: io::Error) -> Self {\n        StoreError::Io(e)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct SeriesState {\n    policy: UnorderedPolicy,\n    block_size: u32,\n    file: active: Vec<Point>,\n    /// High-water timestamp across flushed blocks and active.\n    last_ts: Option<i64>,\n    /// Side buffer for the Buffer policy (never queried).\n    late_buffer: Vec<Point>,\n    /// Compressed bytes (payload + 8-byte record headers) on disk.\n    disk_bytes: u64,\n    /// Points in flushed blocks.\n    flushed_points: u64,\n}\n\n/// The storage engine. Cheaply cloneable (`Arc` inside); methods take `&self`.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Store {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<StoreInner>>,\n}\n\nstruct StoreInner {\n    io: Arc<dyn IoBackend>,\n    root: PathBuf,\n    default_block_size: u32,\n    series: BTreeMap<String, SeriesState>,\n    recover: RecoverReport,\n}\n\nimpl Store {\n    /// Open (or create) a store rooted at `root`, using backend `io`.\n    /// Existing `*.tsb` files are indexed and torn tails truncated.\n    pub fn open(\n        root: impl AsRef<Path>,\n        io: Arc<dyn IoBackend>,\n        default_block_size: u32,\n    ) -> Result<Store, StoreError> {\n        let root = root.as_ref().to_path_buf();\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).map_err(StoreError::Io)?;\n        io.sync_dir(&root)?;\n\n        let mut inner = StoreInner {\n            io,\n            root,\n            default_block_size,\n            series: BTreeMap::new(),\n            recover: RecoverReport::default(),\n        };\n        inner.load_all()?;\n        Ok(Store {\n            inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(inner)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn recovery_report(&self) -> RecoverReport {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().recover.clone()\n    }\n\n    pub fn create_series(\n        &self,\n        name: &str,\n        policy: UnorderedPolicy,\n        block_size: Option<u32>,\n    ) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n        validate_name(name)?;\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        if g.series.contains_key(name) {\n            return Err(StoreError::SeriesExists(name.to_string()));\n        }\n        let bs = block_size.unwrap_or(g.default_block_size).max(1);\n        let path = g.series_path(name);\n        let mut file = g.io.create_new(&path)?;\n        let flags = if matches!(policy, UnorderedPolicy::Buffer) {\n            FLAG_BUFFER\n        } else {\n            0\n        };\n        let mut header = Vec::with_capacity(HEADER_LEN as usize);\n        header.extend_from_slice(MAGIC);\n        header.extend_from_slice(&FORMAT_VERSION.to_le_bytes());\n        header.extend_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());\n        header.extend_from_slice(&bs.to_le_bytes());\n        header.extend_from_slice(&0u64.to_le_bytes()); // reserved\n        file.write_all_at(&header, 0)?;\n        file.sync()?;\n        g.io.sync_dir(&g.root)?;\n\n        g.series.insert(\n            name.to_string(),\n            SeriesState {\n                policy,\n                block_size: bs,\n                file,\n                append_offset: HEADER_LEN,\n                index: Vec::new(),\n                active: Vec::with_capacity(bs as usize),\n                last_ts: None,\n                late_buffer: Vec::new(),\n                disk_bytes: 0,\n                flushed_points: 0,\n            },\n        );\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn list_series(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().series.keys().cloned().collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Append points in batch order. All points in the batch are validated\n    /// against the ordering rule before any are accepted (all-or-nothing).\n    /// Under `Buffer`, any late point is parked instead of failing the batch;\n    /// in-order points are still accepted and may trigger a block flush.\n    pub fn write(&self, name: &str, points: &[Point]) -> Result<WriteOutcome, StoreError> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g\n            .series\n            .get_mut(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(name.to_string()))?;\n\n        // Validate: batch itself must be non-decreasing.\n        let mut prev = s.last_ts;\n        for p in points {\n            if let Some(hw) = prev {\n                if p.ts < hw {\n                    match s.policy {\n                        UnorderedPolicy::Reject => {\n                            return Err(StoreError::OutOfOrder {\n                                ts: p.ts,\n                                last_ts: hw,\n                            });\n                        }\n                        UnorderedPolicy::Buffer => {} // parked below\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            // A buffered point doesn't advance the high-water mark.\n            if prev.map_or(true, |hw| p.ts >= hw) {\n                prev = Some(p.ts);\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut accepted = 0usize;\n        let mut buffered = 0usize;\n        let mut flushed = 0usize;\n        let mut hw = s.last_ts;\n        for p in points {\n            let late = hw.map_or(false, |h| p.ts < h);\n            if late {\n                debug_assert!(matches!(s.policy, UnorderedPolicy::Buffer));\n                s.late_buffer.push(*p);\n                buffered += 1;\n            } else {\n                s.active.push(*p);\n                hw = Some(p.ts);\n                accepted += 1;\n                if s.active.len() as u32 >= s.block_size {\n                    s.flush_active(&g.io, name)?;\n                    flushed += 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        s.last_ts = hw;\n        Ok(WriteOutcome {\n            accepted,\n            buffered,\n            blocks_flushed: flushed,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Force the active points of one series (or all series) into a synced\n    /// block. Returns the number of blocks written.\n    pub fn flush(&self, name: Option<&str>) -> Result<usize, StoreError> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let mut count = 0;\n        match name {\n            Some(n) => {\n                let s = g\n                    .series\n                    .get_mut(n)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(n.to_string()))?;\n                if !s.active.is_empty() {\n                    s.flush_active(&g.io, n)?;\n                    count += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            None => {\n                let names: Vec<String> = g.series.keys().cloned().collect();\n                for n in names {\n                    let s = g.series.get_mut(&n).unwrap();\n                    if !s.active.is_empty() {\n                        s.flush_active(&g.io, &n)?;\n                        count += 1;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(count)\n    }\n\n    /// Merge the side buffer of a `Buffer`-policy series into the ordered\n    /// log. The buffer is stable-sorted by timestamp; insertion stops at the\n    /// first point still older than the high-water mark. Already-merged\n    /// points stay merged; the rest stay buffered.\n    pub fn drain(&self, name: &str) -> Result<DrainOutcome, StoreError> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g\n            .series\n            .get_mut(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(name.to_string()))?;\n\n        s.late_buffer.sort_by(|a, b| a.ts.cmp(&b.ts)); // stable sort\n        let mut merged = Vec::new();\n        let mut accepted = 0usize;\n        let mut remaining = std::mem::take(&mut s.late_buffer);\n        let mut hw = s.last_ts;\n        let mut blocks = 0usize;\n        let mut conflict = None;\n\n        for p in remaining.drain(..) {\n            if hw.map_or(false, |h| p.ts < h) {\n                conflict = Some(p.ts);\n                // This point and every later-buffer point are deferred.\n                s.late_buffer.push(p);\n                break;\n            }\n            s.active.push(p);\n            hw = Some(p.ts);\n            accepted += 1;\n            if s.active.len() as u32 >= s.block_size {\n                s.flush_active(&g.io, name)?;\n                blocks += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        // Anything not consumed remains in the side buffer, preserving order.\n        s.late_buffer.extend(remaining);\n        s.last_ts = hw;\n        let _ = merged;\n        if let Some(ts) = conflict {\n            return Err(StoreError::DrainConflict {\n                accepted,\n                rejected_ts: ts,\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(DrainOutcome {\n            merged: accepted,\n            blocks_flushed: blocks,\n            buffered_remaining: s.late_buffer.len(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn buffered_count(&self, name: &str) -> Result<usize, StoreError> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g\n            .series\n            .get(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(name.to_string()))?;\n        Ok(s.late_buffer.len())\n    }\n\n    /// Range query `[start, end]` (inclusive), in storage order. Only flushed\n    /// blocks whose indexed time range overlaps the window are read from disk\n    /// (binary search on the block index), then filtered; the in-memory\n    /// active block is merged afterwards. Side-buffered points are excluded by\n    /// definition.\n    pub fn query(\n        &self,\n        name: &str,\n        start: i64,\n        end: i64,\n    ) -> Result<QueryReport, StoreError> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g\n            .series\n            .get(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(name.to_string()))?;\n\n        // First block whose last_ts >= start.\n        let first = s\n            .index\n            .partition_point(|m| m.last_ts < start)\n            .min(s.index.len());\n\n        let mut points = Vec::new();\n        let mut blocks_scanned = 0usize;\n        let mut blocks_with_hits = 0usize;\n        let mut bytes_read = 0u64;\n\n        for meta in &s.index[first..] {\n            if meta.first_ts > end {\n                break; // later blocks start even later\n            }\n            blocks_scanned += 1;\n            let mut header = [0u8; 8];\n            read_exact_at(&*s.file, &mut header, meta.record_offset)?;\n            let plen = u32::from_le_bytes(header[0..4].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;\n            let crc_stored = u32::from_le_bytes(header[4..8].try_into().unwrap());\n            if plen != meta.payload_len as usize {\n                return Err(StoreError::Corruption {\n                    series: name.to_string(),\n                    detail: format!(\n                        \"index says payload {} bytes but record says {plen}\",\n                        meta.payload_len\n                    ),\n                });\n            }\n            let mut payload = vec![0u8; plen];\n            read_exact_at(\n                &*s.file,\n                &mut payload,\n                meta.record_offset + 8,\n            )?;\n            bytes_read += 8 + plen as u64;\n            if Crc32::checksum(&payload) != crc_stored {\n                return Err(StoreError::Corruption {\n                    series: name.to_string(),\n                    detail: format!(\"CRC mismatch in block at offset {}\", meta.record_offset),\n                });\n            }\n            let decoded = coding::decode_block(&payload)\n                .map_err(|e| StoreError::Corruption {\n                    series: name.to_string(),\n                    detail: e.to_string(),\n                })?;\n            let before = points.len();\n            points.extend(decoded.into_iter().filter(|p| p.ts >= start && p.ts <= end));\n            if points.len() > before {\n                blocks_with_hits += 1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Merge the active block (already in storage order).\n        points.extend(s.active.iter().copied().filter(|p| p.ts >= start && p.ts <= end));\n\n        Ok(QueryReport {\n            points,\n            blocks_scanned,\n            blocks_with_hits,\n            bytes_read,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Real compression statistics versus an uncompressed 16-byte-per-point\n    /// array (i64 ts + i64 value).\n    pub fn stats(&self, name: &str) -> Result<SeriesStats, StoreError> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g\n            .series\n            .get(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(name.to_string()))?;\n        let flushed_points = s.flushed_points;\n        let active_points = s.active.len() as u64;\n        let buffered = s.late_buffer.len() as u64;\n        let uncompressed = (flushed_points + active_points) * 16;\n        let ratio = if s.disk_bytes == 0 {\n            None\n        } else {\n            Some(uncompressed as f64 / s.disk_bytes as f64)\n        };\n        Ok(SeriesStats {\n            policy: s.policy,\n            block_size: s.block_size,\n            blocks: s.index.len() as u64,\n            flushed_points,\n            active_points,\n            buffered_points: buffered,\n            disk_bytes: s.disk_bytes,\n            uncompressed_bytes: uncompressed,\n            compression_ratio: ratio,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\nfn read_exact_at(\n    file: &dyn crate::io_layer::IoFile,\n    buf: &mut [u8],\n    offset: u64,\n) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n    let mut done = 0;\n    while done < buf.len() {\n        let n = file.read_at(&mut buf[done..], offset + done as u64)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Err(StoreError::Io(io::Error::new(\n                io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof,\n                \"short read from series file\",\n            )));\n        }\n        done += n;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct WriteOutcome {\n    pub accepted: usize,\n    pub buffered: usize,\n    pub blocks_flushed: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct DrainOutcome {\n    pub merged: usize,\n    pub blocks_flushed: usize,\n    pub buffered_remaining: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct QueryReport {\n    pub points: Vec<Point>,\n    pub blocks_scanned: usize,\n    pub blocks_with_hits: usize,\n    pub bytes_read: u64,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct SeriesStats {\n    pub policy: UnorderedPolicy,\n    pub block_size: u32,\n    pub blocks: u64,\n    pub flushed_points: u64,\n    pub active_points: u64,\n    pub buffered_points: u64,\n    pub disk_bytes: u64,\n    pub uncompressed_bytes: u64,\n    pub compression_ratio: Option<f64>,\n}\n\nimpl StoreInner {\n    fn series_path(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n        self.root.join(format!(\"{name}.tsb\"))\n    }\n\n    fn load_all(&mut self) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n        let mut entries: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(&self.root)\n            .map_err(StoreError::Io)?\n            .filter_map(|e| e.ok())\n            .map(|e| e.path())\n            .filter(|p| p.extension().map_or(false, |x| x == \"tsb\"))\n            .collect();\n        entries.sort();\n\n        for path in entries {\n            let name = path\n                .file_stem()\n                .and_then(|s| s.to_str())\n                .unwrap_or_default()\n                .to_string();\n            self.load_one(&path, &name)?;\n            self.recover.series_loaded += 1;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn load_one(&mut self, path: &Path, name: &str) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n        let mut file = self.io.open_write(path)?;\n        let file_len = file.len()?;\n        if file_len < HEADER_LEN {\n            return Err(StoreError::Corruption {\n                series: name.to_string(),\n                detail: \"file shorter than header\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n        let mut header = [0u8; HEADER_LEN as usize];\n        read_exact_at(&*file, &mut header, 0)?;\n        if &header[0..4] != MAGIC {\n            return Err(StoreError::NotAStore);\n        }\n        let version = u16::from_le_bytes(header[4..6].try_into().unwrap());\n        if version != FORMAT_VERSION {\n            return Err(StoreError::UnsupportedVersion(version));\n        }\n        let flags = u16::from_le_bytes(header[6..8].try_into().unwrap());\n        let block_size = u32::from_le_bytes(header[8..12].try_into().unwrap()).max(1);\n        let policy = if flags & FLAG_BUFFER != 0 {\n            UnorderedPolicy::Buffer\n        } else {\n            UnorderedPolicy::Reject\n        };\n\n        // Scan records.\n        let mut index = Vec::new();\n        let mut offset = HEADER_LEN;\n        let mut disk_bytes = 0u64;\n        let mut flushed_points = 0u64;\n        let mut torn = 0usize;\n\n        loop {\n            if offset == file_len {\n                break;\n            }\n            if offset + 8 > file_len {\n                torn += 1;\n                break;\n            }\n            let mut rec_hdr = [0u8; 8];\n            read_exact_at(&*file, &mut rec_hdr, offset)?;\n            let plen = u32::from_le_bytes(rec_hdr[0..4].try_into().unwrap()) as u64;\n            let crc_stored = u32::from_le_bytes(rec_hdr[4..8].try_into().unwrap());\n            if offset + 8 + plen > file_len {\n                torn += 1;\n                break;\n            }\n            let mut payload = vec![0u8; plen as usize];\n            read_exact_at(&*file, &mut payload, offset + 8)?;\n            if Crc32::checksum(&payload) != crc_stored {\n                torn += 1;\n                break;\n            }\n            let decoded = match coding::decode_block(&payload) {\n                Ok(d) => d,\n                Err(_) => {\n                    torn += 1;\n                    break;\n                }\n            };\n            if decoded.is_empty() {\n                torn += 1; // empty blocks are never written; treat as corrupt\n                break;\n            }\n            index.push(BlockMeta {\n                record_offset: offset,\n                payload_len: plen as u32,\n                first_ts: decoded.first().unwrap().ts,\n                last_ts: decoded.last().unwrap().ts,\n                count: decoded.len() as u32,\n            });\n            disk_bytes += 8 + plen;\n            flushed_points += decoded.len() as u64;\n            offset += 8 + plen;\n        }\n\n        let valid_end = offset;\n        if valid_end != file_len {\n            // Drop the torn tail so future appends cannot join onto garbage.\n            file.set_len(valid_end)?;\n            file.sync()?;\n            self.recover.torn_records += torn;\n        }\n\n        let last_ts = index.last().map(|m| m.last_ts);\n        self.recover.blocks_loaded += index.len();\n\n        self.series.insert(\n            name.to_string(),\n            SeriesState {\n                policy,\n                block_size,\n                file,\n                append_offset: valid_end,\n                index,\n                active: Vec::new(),\n                last_ts,\n                late_buffer: Vec::new(),\n                disk_bytes,\n                flushed_points,\n            },\n        );\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SeriesState {\n    /// Encode the active points, append a CRC-framed record, fsync, update\n    /// the in-memory index.\n    fn flush_active(\n        &mut self,\n        io: &Arc<dyn IoBackend>,\n        name: &str,\n    ) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n        if self.active.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let points = std::mem::take(&mut self.active);\n        let payload = coding::encode_block(&points);\n        let crc = Crc32::checksum(&payload);\n\n        let mut record = Vec::with_capacity(8 + payload.len());\n        record.extend_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        record.extend_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());\n        record.extend_from_slice(&payload);\n\n        let offset = self.append_offset;\n        // Write the record then fsync. If either fails, the record may be\n        // partial on disk; recovery will CRC-check and truncate it. We do not\n        // update the index on failure.\n        if let Err(e) = self.file.write_all_at(&record, offset) {\n            // Keep the points so an explicit retry/flush can persist them;\n            // the file region is invalid and will be reclaimed on reopen.\n            self.active = points;\n            return Err(StoreError::Io(e));\n        }\n        if let Err(e) = self.file.sync() {\n            self.active = points;\n            // Also fsync the containing directory? Record appends require no\n            // directory entry change; only data durability matters here.\n            let _ = io;\n            let _ = name;\n            return Err(StoreError::Io(e));\n        }\n\n        self.index.push(BlockMeta {\n            record_offset: offset,\n            payload_len: payload.len() as u32,\n            first_ts: points.first().unwrap().ts,\n            last_ts: points.last().unwrap().ts,\n            count: points.len() as u32,\n        });\n        self.append_offset += record.len() as u64;\n        self.disk_bytes += record.len() as u64;\n        self.flushed_points += points.len() as u64;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Names: 1..=64 chars, ASCII letters/digits/`_`/`-`/`.`, must not start with\n/// `.` or `-`, and must not be `.` / `..`. This maps 1:1 to file names and\n/// rejects path traversal.\npub fn validate_name(name: &str) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n    let ok = !name.is_empty()\n        && name.len() <= 64\n        && name.as_bytes().iter().all(|b| {\n            b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || *b == b'_' || *b == b'-' || *b == b'.'\n        })\n        && !name.starts_with(['.', '-']);\n    if ok {\n        Ok(())\n    } else {\n        Err(StoreError::BadSeriesName(name.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::io_layer::RealIo;\n\n    fn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\n        let d = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n            \"tsblock-test-{}-{}-{}\",\n            tag,\n            std::process::id(),\n            std::time::SystemTime::now()\n                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n                .unwrap()\n                .as_nanos()\n        ));\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();\n        d\n    }\n\n    fn open_store(dir: &Path, bs: u32) -> Store {\n        Store::open(dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), bs).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn name_validation_rules() {\n        assert!(validate_name(\"cpu_0.load\").is_ok());\n        assert!(validate_name(\"a-b_c\").is_ok());\n        assert!(validate_name(\"\").is_err());\n        assert!(validate_name(\"../etc\").is_err());\n        assert!(validate_name(\"a/b\").is_err());\n        assert!(validate_name(\"-dash\").is_err());\n        assert!(validate_name(\".hidden\").is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn write_query_flush_reopen() {\n        let dir = tempdir(\"persist\");\n        let store = open_store(&dir, 4);\n        store.create_series(\"s\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, None).unwrap();\n        let pts: Vec<_> = (0..10).map(|i| Point::new(i, i * 2)).collect();\n        store.write(\"s\", &pts).unwrap();\n        // 10 points, block size 4 -> 2 flushed blocks + 2 active.\n        let r = store.query(\"s\", 2, 7).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(r.points, pts[2..8].to_vec());\n\n        store.flush(None).unwrap();\n        drop(store);\n\n        // Reopen: index rebuilt from disk, torn-tail scan runs.\n        let store2 = open_store(&dir, 4);\n        let rep = store2.recovery_report();\n        assert_eq!(rep.series_loaded, 1);\n        assert_eq!(rep.blocks_loaded, 3);\n        let r = store2.query(\"s\", 2, 7).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(r.points, pts[2..8].to_vec());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reject_policy_blocks_whole_batch() {\n        let dir = tempdir(\"reject\");\n        let store = open_store(&dir, 100);\n        store.create_series(\"s\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, None).unwrap();\n        store.write(\"s\", &[Point::new(1, 1), Point::new(2, 2)]).unwrap();\n        let err = store\n            .write(\"s\", &[Point::new(3, 3), Point::new(0, 0)])\n            .unwrap_err();\n        assert!(matches!(\n            err,\n            StoreError::OutOfOrder {\n                ts: 0,\n                last_ts: 3\n            }\n        ));\n        // Neither
