One series = one file `<data-dir>/<name>.tsb`:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! offset  size  field\n//! 0       4     magic  = b\"TSBK\"\n//! 4       2     version (u16 LE) = 1\n//! 6       2     flags (u16 LE); bit 0: unordered policy (0=reject, 1=buffer)\n//! 8       4     block_size (u32 LE)\n//! 12      8     reserved (8 zero bytes; future index pointer)\n//! 20      ...   records\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Each record:\n//! ```text\n//! payload_len : u32 LE\n//! crc32       : u32 LE   (CRC-32/ISO-HDLC over payload only)\n//! payload     : payload_len bytes, encoded by crate::coding\n//! ```\n//!\n//! A torn trailing record (short header, length overrunning the\n//! file, or CRC mismatch — the signature of a crash or injected ENOSPC\n//! mid-write) ends the scan and is truncated away. A series is created with one of two policies for out-of-order points\n//! (`ts < last accepted ts`; equal timestamps are legal duplicates):\n//!\n//! * `Reject` (default): the whole write batch fails, nothing is accepted.\n//! * `Buffer`: late points go to a separate ordered path (which may reject them again if they are still\n//!   older than the newest accepted point).\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse 1;\npub const HEADER_LEN: u64 = 20;\n\nconst FLAG_BUFFER: u16 = 1;\n\n/// What happens to points whose timestamp is older than the newest point\n/// already accepted by the series.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum UnorderedPolicy {\n    /// Reject the whole batch with [`StoreError::OutOfOrder`].\n    Reject,\n    /// Park late points in a side buffer; merge later with an explicit drain.\n    Buffer,\n}\n\n/// Index entry for one flushed block.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct BlockMeta {\n    /// Absolute offset of the record header (the length field).\n    pub record_offset: u64,\n    pub payload_len: u32,\n    pub first_ts: i64,\n    pub last_ts: i64,\n    pub count: u32,\n}\n\n/// Result of opening a data directory.\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Codec(String),\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for StoreError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StoreError::Io(e) => write!(f, {s:?}\"),\n            StoreError::OutOfOrder { ts, last_ts } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"out-of-order point ts={ts} is older than last accepted ts={last_ts}\"\n            ),\n File-backed block storage engine.\n//!\n//! # On-disk format\n//!\n//! One series = one file `<data-dir>/<name>.tsb`:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! offset  size  field\n//! 0       4     magic  = b\"TSBK\"\n//! 4       2     version (u16 LE) = 1\n//! 6       2     flags (u16 LE); bit 0: unordered policy (0=reject, 1=buffer)\n//! 8       4     block_size (u32 LE)\n//! 12      8     reserved (8 zero bytes; future index pointer)\n//! 20      ...   records\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Each record:\n//! ```text\n//! payload_len : u32 LE\n//! crc32       : u32 LE   (CRC-32/ISO-HDLC over payload only)\n//! payload     : payload_len bytes, encoded by crate::coding\n//! ```\n//!\n//! The block index is **not** stored separately: on open the file is scanned\n//! record by record and an in-memory index (record offset, time range, count)\n//! is rebuilt. A torn trailing record (short header, length overrunning the\n//! file, or CRC mismatch — the signature of a crash or injected ENOSPC\n//! mid-write) ends the scan and is truncated away. This is the durability\n//! boundary:\n//!\n//! * a block is durable only after its record has been fully written **and**\n//!   `fsync`ed;\n//! * points still sitting in the in-memory active block are never durable;\n//! * a failed `fsync` is reported to the client as an error even though bytes\n//!   may be in the page cache — durability was not confirmed.\n//!\n//! # Ordering semantics\n//!\n//! A series is created with one of two policies for out-of-order points\n//! (`ts < last accepted ts`; equal timestamps are legal duplicates):\n//!\n//! * `Reject` (default): the whole write batch fails, nothing is accepted.\n//! * `Buffer`: late points go to a separate in-memory side buffer, are\n//!   excluded from every range query, and are only merged via an explicit\n//!   `drain`, which stable-sorts them by timestamp and inserts them through\n//!   the normal ordered path (which may reject them again if they are still\n//!   older than the newest accepted point).\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::coding::{self, Point};\nuse crate::crc::Crc32;\nuse crate::io_layer::IoBackend;\n\npub const MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b\"TSBK\";\npub const FORMAT_VERSION: u16 = 1;\npub const HEADER_LEN: u64 = 20;\n\nconst FLAG_BUFFER: u16 = 1;\n\n/// What happens to points whose timestamp is older than the newest point\n/// already accepted by the series.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum UnorderedPolicy {\n    /// Reject the whole batch with [`StoreError::OutOfOrder`].\n    Reject,\n    /// Park late points in a side buffer; merge later with an explicit drain.\n    Buffer,\n}\n\n/// Index entry for one flushed block.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct BlockMeta {\n    /// Absolute offset of the record header (the length field).\n    pub record_offset: u64,\n    pub payload_len: u32,\n    pub first_ts: i64,\n    pub last_ts: i64,\n    pub count: u32,\n}\n\n/// Result of opening a data directory.\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]\npub struct RecoverReport {\n    pub series_loaded: usize,\n    pub blocks_loaded: usize,\n    /// Number of trailing torn records truncated away.\n    pub torn_records: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StoreError {\n    Io(io::Error),\n    /// Directory is not a tsblock store (bad/absent magic).\n    NotAStore,\n    /// File header indicates a newer/unsupported format version.\n    UnsupportedVersion(u16),\n    /// Corruption detected away from the tail (CRC failure mid-file).\n    Corruption { series: String, detail: String },\n    SeriesExists(String),\n    UnknownSeries(String),\n    BadSeriesName(String),\n    /// At least one point was older than the series high-water mark.\n    /// Carries the offending timestamp.\n    OutOfOrder { ts: i64, last_ts: i64 },\n    /// Returned when `?policy=buffer` points remain after a failed drain.\n    DrainConflict { accepted: usize, rejected_ts: i64 },\n    Codec(String),\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for StoreError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StoreError::Io(e) => write!(f, \"I/O error: {e}\"),\n            StoreError::NotAStore => write!(f, \"not a tsblock data directory\"),\n            StoreError::UnsupportedVersion(v) => write!(f, \"unsupported format version {v}\"),\n            StoreError::Corruption { series, detail } => {\n                write!(f, \"corruption in series {series}: {detail}\")\n            }\n            StoreError::SeriesExists(s) => write!(f, \"series {s:?} already exists\"),\n            StoreError::UnknownSeries(s) => write!(f, \"unknown series {s:?}\"),\n            StoreError::BadSeriesName(s) => write!(f, \"bad series name {s:?}\"),\n            StoreError::OutOfOrder { ts, last_ts } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"out-of-order point ts={ts} is older than last accepted ts={last_ts}\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::DrainConflict {\n                accepted,\n                rejected_ts,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"drain stopped after {accepted} point(s) at still-late ts={rejected_ts}\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::Codec(s) => write!(f, \"codec error: {s}\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StoreError {}\n\nimpl From<io::Error> for StoreError {\n    fn from(e: io::Error) -> Self {\n        StoreError::Io(e)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct SeriesState {\n    policy: UnorderedPolicy,\n    block_size: u32,\n    file: Box<dyn crate::io_layer::IoFile>,\n    /// End of the valid region; next record is appended here.\n    append_offset: u64,\n    index: Vec<BlockMeta>,\n    /// Ordered, not-yet-flushed points.\n    active: Vec<Point>,\n    /// High-water timestamp across flushed blocks and active.\n    last_ts: Option<i64>,\n    /// Side buffer for the Buffer policy (never queried).\n    late_buffer: Vec<Point>,\n    /// Compressed bytes (payload + 8-byte record headers) on disk.\n    disk_bytes: u64,\n    /// Points in flushed blocks.\n    flushed_points: u64,\n}\n\n/// The storage engine. Cheaply cloneable (`Arc` inside); methods take `&self`.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Store {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<StoreInner>>,\n}\n\nstruct StoreInner {\n    io: Arc<dyn IoBackend>,\n    root: PathBuf,\n    default_block_size: u32,\n    series: BTreeMap<String, SeriesState>,\n    recover: RecoverReport,\n}\n\nimpl Store {\n    /// Open (or create) a store rooted at `root`, using backend `io`.\n    /// Existing `*.tsb` files are indexed and torn tails truncated.\n    pub fn open(\n        root: impl AsRef<Path>,\n        io: Arc<dyn IoBackend>,\n        default_block_size: u32,\n    ) -> Result<Store, StoreError> {\n        let root = root.as_ref().to_path_buf();\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).map_err(StoreError::Io)?;\n        io.sync_dir(&root)?;\n\n        let mut inner = StoreInner {\n            io,\n            root,\n            default_block_size,\n            series: BTreeMap::new(),\n            recover: RecoverReport::default(),\n        };\n        inner.load_all()?;\n        Ok(Store {\n            inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(inner)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn recovery_report(&self) -> RecoverReport {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().recover.clone()\n    }\n\n    pub fn create_series(\n        &self,\n        name: &str,\n        policy: UnorderedPolicy,\n        block_size: Option<u32>,\n    ) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n        validate_name(name)?;\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        if g.series.contains_key(name) {\n            return Err(StoreError::SeriesExists(name.to_string()));\n        }\n        let bs = block_size.unwrap_or(g.default_block_size).max(1);\n        let path = g.series_path(name);\n        let mut file = g.io.create_new(&path)?;\n        let flags = if matches!(policy, UnorderedPolicy::Buffer) {\n            FLAG_BUFFER\n        } else {\n            0\n        };\n        let mut header = Vec::with_capacity(HEADER_LEN as usize);\n        header.extend_from_slice(MAGIC);\n        header.extend_from_slice(&FORMAT_VERSION.to_le_bytes());\n        header.extend_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());\n        header.extend_from_slice(&bs.to_le_bytes());\n        header.extend_from_slice(&0u64.to_le_bytes()); // reserved\n        file.write_all_at(&header, 0)?;\n        file.sync()?;\n        g.io.sync_dir(&g.root)?;\n\n        g.series.insert(\n            name.to_string(),\n            SeriesState {\n                policy,\n                block_size: bs,\n                file,\n                append_offset: HEADER_LEN,\n                index: Vec::new(),\n                active: Vec::with_capacity(bs as usize),\n                last_ts: None,\n                late_buffer: Vec::new(),\n                disk_bytes: 0,\n                flushed_points: 0,\n            },\n        );\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn list_series(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().series.keys().cloned().collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Append points in batch order. All points in the batch are validated\n    /// against the ordering rule before any are accepted (all-or-nothing).\n    /// Under `Buffer`, any late point is parked instead of failing the batch;\n    /// in-order points are still accepted and may trigger a block flush.\n    pub fn write(&self, name: &str, points: &[Point]) -> Result<WriteOutcome, StoreError> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g\n            .series\n            .get_mut(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(name.to_string()))?;\n\n        // Validate: batch itself must be non-decreasing.\n        let mut prev = s.last_ts;\n        for p in points {\n            if let Some(hw) = prev {\n                if p.ts < hw {\n                    match s.policy {\n                        UnorderedPolicy::Reject => {\n                            return Err(StoreError::OutOfOrder {\n                                ts: p.ts,\n                                last_ts: hw,\n                            });\n                        }\n                        UnorderedPolicy::Buffer => {} // parked below\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            // A buffered point doesn't advance the high-water mark.\n            if prev.map_or(true, |hw| p.ts >= hw) {\n                prev = Some(p.ts);\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut accepted = 0usize;\n        let mut buffered = 0usize;\n        let mut flushed = 0usize;\n        let mut hw = s.last_ts;\n        for p in points {\n            let late = hw.map_or(false, |h| p.ts < h);\n            if late {\n                debug_assert!(matches!(s.policy, UnorderedPolicy::Buffer));\n                s.late_buffer.push(*p);\n                buffered += 1;\n            } else {\n                s.active.push(*p);\n                hw = Some(p.ts);\n                accepted += 1;\n                if s.active.len() as u32 >= s.block_size {\n                    s.flush_active(&g.io, name)?;\n                    flushed += 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        s.last_ts = hw;\n        Ok(WriteOutcome {\n            accepted,\n            buffered,\n            blocks_flushed: flushed,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Force the active points of one series (or all series) into a synced\n    /// block. Returns the number of blocks written.\n    pub fn flush(&self, name: Option<&str>) -> Result<usize, StoreError> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let mut count = 0;\n        match name {\n            Some(n) => {\n                let s = g\n                    .series\n                    .get_mut(n)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(n.to_string()))?;\n                if !s.active.is_empty() {\n                    s.flush_active(&g.io, n)?;\n                    count += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            None => {\n                let names: Vec<String> = g.series.keys().cloned().collect();\n                for n in names {\n                    let s = g.series.get_mut(&n).unwrap();\n                    if !s.active.is_empty() {\n                        s.flush_active(&g.io, &n)?;\n                        count += 1;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(count)\n    }\n\n    /// Merge the side buffer of a `Buffer`-policy series into the ordered\n    /// log. The buffer is stable-sorted by timestamp; insertion stops at the\n    /// first point still older than the high-water mark. Already-merged\n    /// points stay merged; the rest stay buffered.\n    pub fn drain(&self, name: &str) -> Result<DrainOutcome, StoreError> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g\n            .series\n            .get_mut(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(name.to_string()))?;\n\n        s.late_buffer.sort_by(|a, b| a.ts.cmp(&b.ts)); block whose last_ts >= start.\n        let first = s\n            .index\n            .partition_point(|m| m.last_ts < start)\n            .min(s.index.len());\n\n        let mut points = Vec::new();\n        let mut blocks_scanned = 0usize;\n        let mut blocks_with_hits = 0usize;\n        let mut bytes_read = 0u64;\n\n        for meta in &s.index[first..] {\n            if u32::from_le_bytes(header[4..8].try_into().unwrap());\n            if plen != meta.payload_len as usize {\n                return Err(StoreError::Corruption {\n                    series: blocks_with_hits += 1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Merge the active block (already in storage order).\n        points.extend(s.active.iter().copied().filter(|p| p.ts >= start && p.ts <= {"parentUuid":"b0aa2ee0-2909-47af-8769-6f33eb527faa","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_r0k5dtm02g4q328zpnfwres4","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp7/b/src/server.rs","content":"//! Minimal std-only HTTP/1.1 verification surface.\n//!\n//! This is intentionally not a general-purpose web framework: one connection\n//! per request, no keep-alive, tiny routing table. It exists to exercise the\n//! storage engine over a real local socket so acceptance checks can use plain\n//! HTTP. All payloads use simple line protocols rather than pulling in a JSON\n//! parser; responses are hand-emitted JSON.\n//!\n//! ## Routes\n//!\n//! | Method | Path                                   | Meaning |\n//! |--------|----------------------------------------|---------|\n//! | GET    | `/health`                              | liveness |\n//! | GET    | `/series`                              | list series |\n//! | POST   | `/series/{name}?policy=&block_size=`   | create series |\n//! | GET    | `/series/{name}/stats`                 | compression stats |\n//! | POST   | `/series/{name}/points?sync=`          | append `ts,value` lines |\n//! | GET    | `/series/{name}/range?start=&end=`     | inclusive range query |\n//! | POST   | `/series/{name}/flush`                 | fsync active block |\n//! | POST   | `/series/{name}/drain`                 | merge buffered late points |\n//! | GET    | `/series/{name}/buffered`              | count of late-buffered points |\n//! | POST   | `/dev/fault`                           | inject I/O faults (line body) |\n//!\n//! Write body lines are `timestamp,value` (both signed i64), separated by\n//! `\\n`; blank lines are ignored. `sync=true` forces a flush+fsync before the\n//! response is returned (default: flush automatically only at block size).\n//!\n//! Fault body lines: `write_limit=<bytes>`, `fail_syncs=<n>`, `clear`.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\n\nuse crate::coding::Point;\nuse crate::io_layer::{FaultRules, FaultyIo, RealIo};\nuse crate::store::{self, Store, StoreError, UnorderedPolicy};\n\n/// Shared server state.\npub struct AppState {\n    pub store: Store,\n    pub fault_rules: Option<Arc<FaultRules>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FaultMode {\n    Off,\n    On,\n}\n\n/// Parse and bind a server. With [`FaultMode::On`] the store runs behind a\n/// [`FaultyIo`] backend and `/dev/fault` is live; without it, the route\n/// returns 404.\npub fn serve(\n    addr: &str,\n    data_dir: PathBuf,\n    block_size: u32,\n    fault_mode: FaultMode,\n) -> std::io::Result<ServerHandle> {\n    let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)?;\n    let local_addr = listener.local_addr()?;\n\n    let state = match fault_mode {\n        FaultMode::Off => {\n            let store = Store::open(&data_dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), block_size)\n                .map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;\n            Arc::new(AppState {\n                store,\n                fault_rules: None,\n            })\n        }\n        FaultMode::On => {\n            let rules = Arc::new(FaultRules::new());\n            let io = Arc::new(FaultyIo::new(Arc::new(RealIo::new()), Arc::clone(&rules)));\n            let store = Store::open(&data_dir, io, block_size).map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;\n            Arc::new(AppState {\n                store,\n                fault_rules: Some(rules),\n            })\n        }\n    };\n\n    let handle = ServerHandle {\n        addr: local_addr,\n        stop: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)),\n    };\n    let stop_flag = Arc::clone(&handle.stop);\n\n    std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        listener\n            .set_nonblocking(true)\n            .expect(\"set_nonblocking on listener\");\n        while !stop_flag.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {\n            match listener.accept() {\n                Ok((stream, _peer)) => {\n                    let state = Arc::clone(&state);\n                    // Handle each connection on its own short-lived thread.\n                    std::thread::spawn(move || {\n                        let _ = handle_connection(stream, state);\n                    });\n                }\n                Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {\n                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(5));\n                }\n                Err(_) => break,\n            }\n        }\n    });\n\n    Ok(handle)\n}\n\npub struct ServerHandle {\n    addr: std::net::SocketAddr,\n    stop: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>,\n}\n\nimpl ServerHandle {\n    pub fn addr(&self) -> std::net::SocketAddr {\n        self.addr\n    }\n\n    pub fn port(&self) -> u16 {\n        self.addr.port()\n    }\n\n    pub fn shutdown(&self) {\n        self.stop\n            .store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for ServerHandle {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        self.shutdown();\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Connection handling\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nstruct Request {\n    method: String,\n    path: String, // path portion only\n    query: String,\n    body: String,\n}\n\nfn handle_connection(mut stream: TcpStream, state: Arc<AppState>) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)))?;\n    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)))?;\n\n    // Read until end of headers, accumulating up to 1 MiB.\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(2048);\n    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];\n    let mut header_end = None;\n    while header_end.is_none() && buf.len() < 1024 * 1024 {\n        match stream.read(&mut byte) {\n            Ok(0) => break,\n            Ok(_) => {\n                buf.push(byte[0]);\n                if buf.len() >= 4 && &buf[buf.len() - 4..] == b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\" {\n                    header_end = Some(buf.len());\n                } else if buf.len() >= 2 && &buf[buf.len() - 2..] == b\"\\n\\n\" {\n                    header_end = Some(buf.len());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => break,\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n    let header_end = match header_end {\n        Some(n) => n,\n        None => {\n            return send_simple(&mut stream, 400, \"malformed request (no header end)\");\n        }\n    };\n\n    let header_text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..header_end]).to_string();\n    let mut lines = header_text.split(\"\\r\\n\").filter(|l| !l.is_empty());\n    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let mut parts = request_line.split_whitespace();\n    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n    let target = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let (path, query) = match target.split_once('?') {\n        Some((p, q)) => (p.to_string(), q.to_string()),\n        None => (target.to_string(), String::new()),\n    };\n    let content_length: usize = header_text\n        .lines()\n        .find_map(|line| {\n            let lower = line.to_ascii_lowercase();\n            lower\n                .strip_prefix(\"content-length:\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse().ok())\n        })\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n\n    let mut body = String::new();\n    if content_length > 0 {\n        // Remaining bytes after the header terminator.\n        let already = buf.len() - header_end;\n        let mut rest = vec![0u8; content_length.saturating_sub(already)];\n        stream.read_exact(&mut rest)?;\n        let mut all = buf[header_end..].to_vec();\n        all.extend_from_slice(&rest);\n        all.truncate(content_length);\n        body = String::from_utf8_lossy(&all).to_string();\n    }\n\n    let req = Request {\n        method,\n        path,\n        query,\n        body,\n    };\n    let (status, json) = route(&req, &state);\n    send_response(&mut stream, status, &json)\n}\n\nfn send_simple(stream: &mut TcpStream, status: u16, msg: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let body = format!(\n        \"{{\\\"ok\\\":{},\\\"error\\\":{}}}\",\n        status == 200,\n        json_string(msg)\n    );\n    send_response(stream, status, &body)\n}\n\nfn send_response(stream: &mut TcpStream, status: u16, body: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let reason = reason_phrase(status);\n    let head = format!(\n        \"HTTP/1.1 {status} {reason}\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\",\n        body.len()\n    );\n    stream.write_all(head.as_bytes())?;\n    stream.write_all(body.as_bytes())?;\n    stream.flush()\n}\n\nfn reason_phrase(status: u16) -> &'static str {\n    match status {\n        200 => \"OK\",\n        201 => \"Created\",\n        400 => \"Bad Request\",\n        404 => \"Not Found\",\n        409 => \"Conflict\",\n        500 => \"Internal Server Error\",\n        _ => \"OK\",\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Routing\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nfn route(req: &Request, state: &AppState) -> (u16, String) {\n    match try_route(req, state) {\n        Ok((status, body)) => (status, body),\n        Err((status, msg)) => (\n            status,\n            format!(\"{{\\\"ok\\\":false,\\\"error\\\":{}}}\", json_string(&msg)),\n        ),\n    }\n}\n\ntype RouteResult = Result<(u16, String), (u16, String)>;\n\nfn err(status: u16, msg: impl Into<String>) -> RouteResult {\n    Err((status, msg.into()))\n}\n\nfn try_route(req: &Request, state: &AppState) -> RouteResult {\n    let path = req.path.trim_end_matches('/');\n\n    if path == \"/health\" && req.method == \"GET\" {\n        return Ok((\n            200,\n            format!(\n                \"{{\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"time_ms\\\":{}}}\",\n                SystemTime::now()\n                    .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n                    .map(|d| d.as_millis())\n                    .unwrap_or(0)\n            ),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    if path == \"/series\" && req.method == \"GET\" {\n        let names = state.store.list_series();\n        let arr = names\n            .iter()\n            .map(|n| json_string(n))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\",\");\n        return Ok((200, format!(\"{{\\\"series\\\":[{arr}]}}\")));\n    }\n\n    if path == \"/dev/fault\" && req.method == \"POST\" {\n        let rules = state\n            .fault_rules\n            .as_ref()\n            .ok_or_else(|| (404, \"fault injection disabled (start server with --fault)\".to_string()))?;\n        for line in req.body.lines().map(str::trim).filter(|l| !l.is_empty()) {\n            if line == \"clear\" {\n                rules.clear();\n            } else if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix(\"write_limit=\") {\n                if v == \"none\" {\n                    rules.clear();\n                } else {\n                    let limit: u64 = parse_i64(v)\n                        .and_then(|x| u64::try_from(x).ok())\n                        .map_err(|_| (400, format!(\"bad write_limit: {v}\")))?;\n                    rules.fail_writes_after(limit);\n                }\n            } else if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix(\"fail_syncs=\") {\n                let n: usize = v\n                    .parse()\n                    .map_err(|_| (400, format!(\"bad fail_syncs: {v}\")))?;\n                rules.fail_next_syncs(n);\n            } else {\n                return err(400, format!(\"unknown fault directive: {line}\"));\n            }\n        }\n        return Ok((\n            200,\n            format!(\n                \"{{\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"bytes_written\\\":{}}}\",\n                rules.bytes_written()\n            ),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // Series-scoped routes.\n    if let Some(rest) = path.strip_prefix(\"/series/\") {\n        let segments: Vec<&str> = rest.split('/').collect();\n        return match segments.as_slice() {\n            [name] if req.method == \"POST\" => create_series(state, name, &req.query),\n            [name, \"stats\"] if req.method == \"GET\" => series_stats(state, name),\n            [name, \"points\"] if req.method == \"POST\" => write_points(state, name, &req.query, &req.body),\n            [name, \"range\"] if req.method == \"GET\" => range_query(state, name, &req.query),\n            [name, \"flush\"] if req.method == \"POST\" => flush_series(state, name),\n            [name, \"drain\"] if req.method == \"POST\" => drain_series(state, name),\n            [name, \"buffered\"] if req.method == \"GET\" => buffered_count(state, name),\n            _ => err(404, format!(\"no such route: {} {}\", req.method, req.path)),\n        };\n    }\n\n    err(404, format!(\"no such route: {} {}\", req.method, req.path))\n}\n\nfn create_series(state: &AppState, name: &str, query: &str) -> RouteResult {\n    let params = parse_query(query);\n    let policy = match params.get(\"policy\").copied().unwrap_or(\"reject\") {\n        \"reject\" => UnorderedPolicy::Reject,\n        \"buffer\" => UnorderedPolicy::Buffer,\n        other => return err(400, format!(\"unknown policy: {other}\")),\n    };\n    let block_size = match params.get(\"block_size\") {\n        Some(v) => Some(\n            v.parse::<u32>()\n                .map_err(|_| (400, format!(\"bad block_size: {v}\")))?\n                .max(1),\n        ),\n        None => None,\n    };\n    state\n        .store\n        .create_series(name, policy, block_size)\n        .map_err(store_err_status)?;\n    Ok((\n        201,\n        format!(\n            \"{{\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"series\\\":{},\\\"policy\\\":\\\"{}\\\"}}\",\n            json_string(name),\n            if matches!(policy, UnorderedPolicy::Buffer) {\n                \"buffer\"\n            } else {\n                \"reject\"\n            }\n        ),\n    ))\n}\n\nfn series_stats(state: &AppState, name: &str) -> RouteResult {\n    let s = state.store.stats(name).map_err(store_err_status)?;\n    Ok((\n        200,\n        format!(\n            \"{{\\\"series\\\":{},\\\"policy\\\":\\\"{}\\\",\\\"block_size\\\":{},\\\"blocks\\\":{},\\\"flushed_points\\\":{},\\\"active_points\\\":{},\\\"buffered_points\\\":{},\\\"disk_bytes\\\":{},\\\"uncompressed_bytes\\\":{},\\\"compression_ratio\\\":{}}}\",\n            json_string(name),\n            if matches!(s.policy, UnorderedPolicy::Buffer) { \"buffer\" } else { \"reject\" },\n            s.block_size,\n            s.blocks,\n            s.flushed_points,\n            s.active_points,\n            s.buffered_points,\n            s.disk_bytes,\n            s.uncompressed_bytes,\n            match s.compression_ratio {\n                Some(r) => format!(\"{r:.6}\"),\n                None => \"null\".to_string(),\n            }\n        ),\n    ))\n}\n\nfn write_points(state: &AppState, name: &str, query: &str, body: &str) -> RouteResult {\n    let mut points = Vec::new();\n    for (i, line) in body.lines().map(str::trim).enumerate() {\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let (ts_s, v_s) = line\n            .split_once(',')\n            .ok_or_else(|| (400, format!(\"line {}: expected `ts,value`\", i + 1)))?;\n        let ts = parse_i64(ts_s.trim()).map_err(|_| (400, format!(\"line {}: bad ts\", i + 1)))?;\n        let value = parse_i64(v_s.trim()).map_err(|_| (400, format!(\"line {}: bad value\", i + 1)))?;\n        points.push(Point::new(ts, value));\n    }\n    if points.is_empty() {\n        return err(400, \"empty batch\");\n    }\n\n    let outcome = state\n        .store\n        .write(name, &points)\n        .map_err(store_err_status)?;\n\n    let sync = parse_query(query)\n        .get(\"sync\")\n        .map(|v| *v == \"true\" || *v == \"1\")\n        .unwrap_or(false);\n    let mut flushed = outcome.blocks_flushed;\n    if sync {\n        flushed += state.store.flush(Some(name)).map_err(store_err_status)?;\n    }\n\n    Ok((\n        200,\n        format!(\n            \"{{\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"accepted\\\":{},\\\"buffered\\\":{},\\\"blocks_flushed\\\":{}}}\",\n            outcome.accepted, outcome.buffered, flushed\n        ),\n    ))\n}\n\nfn range_query(state: &AppState, name: &str, query: &str) -> RouteResult {\n    let params = parse_query(query);\n    let start = params\n        .get(\"start\")\n        .copied()\n        .ok_or_else(|| (400, \"missing `start`\".to_string()))\n        .and_then(|v| parse_i64(v).map_err(|_| (400, format!(\"bad start: {v}\"))))?;\n    let end = params\n        .get(\"end\")\n        .copied()\n        .ok_or_else(|| (400, \"missing `end`\".to_string()))\n        .and_then(|v| parse_i64(v).map_err(|_| (400, format!(\"bad end: {v}\"))))?;\n    if start > end {\n        return err(400, \"start > end\");\n    }\n\n    let report = state.store.query(name, start, end).map_err(store_err_status)?;\n    let arr = report\n        .points\n        .iter()\n        .map(|p| format!(\"[{},{}]\", p.ts, p.value))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\",\");\n    Ok((\n        200,\n        format!(\n            \"{{\\\"series\\\":{},\\\"start\\\":{start},\\\"end\\\":{end},\\\"count\\\":{},\\\"blocks_scanned\\\":{},\\\"blocks_with_hits\\\":{},\\\"bytes_read\\\":{},\\\"points\\\":[{arr}]}}\",\n            json_string(name),\n            report.points.len(),\n            report.blocks_scanned,\n            report.blocks_with_hits,\n            report.bytes_read\n        ),\n    ))\n}\n\nfn flush_series(state: &AppState, name: &str) -> RouteResult {\n    let n = state.store.flush(Some(name)).map_err(store_err_status)?;\n    Ok((200, format!(\"{{\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"blocks_flushed\\\":{n}}}\")))\n}\n\nfn drain_series(state: &AppState, name: &str) -> RouteResult {\n    match state.store.drain(name) {\n        Ok(d) => Ok((\n            200,\n            format!(\n                \"{{\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"merged\\\":{},\\\"blocks_flushed\\\":{},\\\"buffered_remaining\\\":{}}}\",\n                d.merged, d.blocks_flushed, d.buffered_remaining\n            ),\n        )),\n        Err(StoreError::DrainConflict {\n            accepted,\n            rejected_ts,\n        }) => Ok((\n            409,\n            format!(\n                \"{{\\\"ok\\\":false,\\\"error\\\":{},\\\"merged\\\":{accepted},\\\"rejected_ts\\\":{rejected_ts}}}\",\n                json_string(\"drain conflict: point still older than high-water mark\")\n            ),\n        )),\n        Err(e) => Err(store_err_status(e)),\n    }\n}\n\nfn buffered_count(state: &AppState, name: &str) -> RouteResult {\n    let n = state\n        .store\n        .buffered_count(name)\n        .map_err(store_err_status)?;\n    Ok((200, format!(\"{{\\\"series\\\":{},\\\"buffered\\\":{n}}}\", json_string(name))))\n}\n\nfn store_err_status(e: StoreError) -> (u16, String) {\n    let status = match &e {\n        StoreError::UnknownSeries(_) => 404,\n        StoreError::SeriesExists(_) | StoreError::OutOfOrder { .. } | StoreError::DrainConflict { .. } => 409,\n        StoreError::BadSeriesName(_)\n        | StoreError::NotAStore\n        | StoreError::UnsupportedVersion(_)\n        | StoreError::Codec(_) => 400,\n        StoreError::Corruption { .. } => 500,\n        StoreError::Io(ioe) => {\n            use std::io::ErrorKind::*;\n            match ioe.kind() {\n                NotFound => 404,\n                PermissionDenied => 403,\n                _ => 500,\n            }\n        }\n    };\n    (status, e.to_string())\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Small parsing/formatting helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nfn parse_query(query: &str) -> Vec<(&str, &str)> {\n    query\n        .split('&')\n        .filter(|p| !p.is_empty())\n        .filter_map(|p| p.split_once('='))\n        .map(|(k, v)| (k, v))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Strict signed i64 decimal parse (optional leading `-`, digits only,\n/// range-checked). Rejects `+`, whitespace, underscores and overflow.\nfn parse_i64(s: &str) -> Result<i64, ()> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    if s.is_empty() {\n        return Err(());\n    }\n    let (neg, digits) = match s.strip_prefix('-') {\n        Some(rest) => (true, rest),\n        None => (false, s),\n    };\n    if digits.is_empty() || !digits.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) {\n        return Err(());\n    }\n    let mut value: i128 = 0;\n    for b in digits.bytes() {\n        value = value * 10 + (b - b'0') as i128;\n        if value > i64::MAX as i128 + neg as i128 {\n            return Err(());\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(if neg { -(value as i64) } else { value as i64 })\n}\n\n/// Minimal JSON string escaper for the characters that must be escaped.\nfn json_string(s: &str) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len() + 2);\n    out.push('\"');\n    for c in s.chars() {\n        match c {\n            '\"' => out.push_str(\"\\\\\\\"\"),\n            '\\\\' => out.push_str(\"\\\\\\\\\"),\n            '\\n' => out.push_str(\"\\\\n\"),\n            '\\r' => out.push_str(\"\\\\r\"),\n            '\\t' => out.push_str(\"\\\\t\"),\n            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => out.push_str(&format!(\"\\\\u{:04x}\", c as u32)),\n            c => out.push(c),\n        }\n    }\n    out.push('\"');\n    out\n}\n\n/// Convenience for integration tests: perform one request over a real socket.\npub fn raw_request(addr: std::net::SocketAddr, raw: &str) -> (u16, String) {\n    use std::io::Read as _;\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).unwrap();\n    stream.write_all(raw.as_bytes()).unwrap();\n    let mut data = Vec::new();\n    stream.read_to_end(&mut data).unwrap();\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&data);\n    let status = text\n        .split_whitespace()\n        .nth(1)\n        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n    let body = text.split(\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\").nth(1).unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n    (status, body)\n}\n\n/// JSON-body POST helper for tests / scripts.\npub fn post(addr: std::net::SocketAddr, path: &str, body: &str) -> (u16, String) {\n    let raw = format!(\n        \"POST {path} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nContent-Type: text/plain\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n{body}\",\n        body.len()\n    );\n    raw_request(addr, &raw)\n}\n\npub fn get(addr: std::net::SocketAddr, path: &str) -> (u16, String) {\n    let raw = format!(\"GET {path} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\");\n    raw_request(addr, &raw)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_i64_strict() {\n        assert_eq!(parse_i64(\"0\"), Ok(0));\n        assert_eq!(parse_i64(\"-1\"), Ok(-1));\n        assert_eq!(parse_i64(\"9223372036854775807\"), Ok(i64::MAX));\n        assert_eq!(parse_i64(\"-9223372036854775808\"), Ok(i64::MIN));\n        assert!(parse_i64(\"9223372036854775808\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse_i64(\"-9223372036854775809\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse_i64(\"\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse_i64(\"1.0\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse_i64(\"+1\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse_i64(\" 1\").is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn json_escape() {\n        assert_eq!(json_string(\"a\\\"b\\\\c\"), \"\\\"a\\\\\\\"b\\\\\\\\c\\\"\");\n        assert_eq!(json_string(\"x\\ny\"), \"\\\"x\\\\ny\\\"\");\n    }\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_5d47883ecab4a94e3dab84c4","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":872,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":68408,"output_tokens":6883,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_r0k5dtm02g4q328zpnfwres4":{"content":"//! Minimal std-only HTTP/1.1 verification surface.\n//!\n//! This is intentionally not a general-purpose web framework: one connection\n//! per request, no keep-alive, tiny routing table. It exists to exercise the\n//! storage engine over a real local socket so acceptance checks can use plain\n//! HTTP. All payloads use simple line protocols rather than pulling in a JSON\n//! parser; responses are hand-emitted JSON.\n//!\n//! ## Routes\n//!\n//! | Method | Path                                   | Meaning |\n//! |--------|----------------------------------------|---------|\n//! | GET    | `/health`                              | liveness |\n//! | GET    | `/series`                              | list series |\n//! | POST   | `/series/{name}?policy=&block_size=`   | create series |\n//! | GET    | `/series/{name}/stats`                 | compression stats |\n//! | POST   | `/series/{name}/points?sync=`          | append `ts,value` lines |\n//! | GET    | `/series/{name}/range?start=&end=`     | inclusive range query |\n//! | POST   | `/series/{name}/flush`                 | fsync active block |\n//! | POST   | `/series/{name}/drain`                 | merge buffered late points |\n//! | GET    | `/series/{name}/buffered`              | count of late-buffered points |\n//! | POST   | `/dev/fault`                           | inject I/O faults (line body) |\n//!\n//! Write body lines are `timestamp,value` (both signed i64), separated by\n//! `\\n`; blank lines are ignored. `sync=true` forces a flush+fsync before the\n//! response is returned (default: flush automatically only at block size).\n//!\n//! Fault body lines: `write_limit=<bytes>`, `fail_syncs=<n>`, `clear`.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\n\nuse crate::coding::Point;\nuse crate::io_layer::{FaultRules, FaultyIo, RealIo};\nuse crate::store::{self, Store, StoreError, UnorderedPolicy};\n\n/// Shared server state.\npub struct AppState {\n    pub store: Store,\n    pub fault_rules: Option<Arc<FaultRules>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FaultMode {\n    Off,\n    On,\n}\n\n/// Parse and bind a server. With [`FaultMode::On`] the store runs behind a\n/// [`FaultyIo`] backend and `/dev/fault` is live; without it, the route\n/// returns 404.\npub fn serve(\n    addr: &str,\n    data_dir: PathBuf,\n    block_size: u32,\n    fault_mode: FaultMode,\n) -> std::io::Result<ServerHandle> {\n    let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)?;\n    let local_addr = listener.local_addr()?;\n\n    let state = match fault_mode {\n        FaultMode::Off => {\n            let store = Store::open(&data_dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), block_size)\n                .map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;\n            Arc::new(AppState {\n                store,\n                fault_rules: None,\n            })\n        }\n        FaultMode::On => {\n            let rules = Arc::new(FaultRules::new());\n            let io = Arc::new(FaultyIo::new(Arc::new(RealIo::new()), Arc::clone(&rules)));\n            let store = Store::open(&data_dir, io, block_size).map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;\n            Arc::new(AppState {\n                store,\n                fault_rules: Some(rules),\n            })\n        }\n    };\n\n    let handle = ServerHandle {\n        addr: local_addr,\n        stop: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)),\n    };\n    let stop_flag = Arc::clone(&handle.stop);\n\n    std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        listener\n            .set_nonblocking(true)\n            .expect(\"set_nonblocking on listener\");\n        while !stop_flag.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {\n            match listener.accept() {\n                Ok((stream, _peer)) => Fault body lines: `write_limit=<bytes>`, `fail_syncs=<n>`, `clear`.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\n\nuse crate::coding::Point;\nuse crate::io_layer::{FaultRules, FaultyIo, RealIo};\nuse crate::store::{self, Store, StoreError, UnorderedPolicy};\n\n/// Shared server state.\npub struct AppState {\n    pub store: Store,\n    pub fault_rules: Option<Arc<FaultRules>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FaultMode {\n    Off,\n    On,\n}\n\n/// Parse and bind a server. With [`FaultMode::On`] the store runs behind a\n/// [`FaultyIo`] backend and `/dev/fault` is live; without it, the route\n/// returns 404.\npub fn serve(\n    addr: &str,\n    data_dir: PathBuf,\n    block_size: u32,\n    fault_mode: FaultMode,\n) -> std::io::Result<ServerHandle> {\n    let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)?;\n    let local_addr = listener.local_addr()?;\n\n    let state = match fault_mode {\n        FaultMode::Off => {\n            let store = Store::open(&data_dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), block_size)\n                .map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;\n            Arc::new(AppState {\n                store,\n                fault_rules: None,\n            })\n        }\n        FaultMode::On => {\n            let rules = Arc::new(FaultRules::new());\n            let io = Arc::new(FaultyIo::new(Arc::new(RealIo::new()), Arc::clone(&rules)));\n            let store = Store::open(&data_dir, io, block_size).map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;\n            Arc::new(AppState {\n                store,\n                fault_rules: Some(rules),\n            })\n        }\n    };\n\n    let handle = ServerHandle {\n        addr: local_addr,\n        stop: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)),\n    };\n    let stop_flag = Arc::clone(&handle.stop);\n\n    std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        listener\n            .set_nonblocking(true)\n            .expect(\"set_nonblocking on listener\");\n        while !stop_flag.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {\n            match listener.accept() {\n                Ok((stream, _peer)) => {\n                    let state = Arc::clone(&state);\n                    // Handle each connection on its own short-lived thread.\n                    std::thread::spawn(move || {\n                        let _ = handle_connection(stream, state);\n                    });\n                }\n                Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {\n                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(5));\n                }\n                Err(_) => break,\n            }\n        }\n    });\n\n    Ok(handle)\n}\n\npub struct ServerHandle {\n    addr: std::net::SocketAddr,\n    stop: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>,\n}\n\nimpl ServerHandle {\n    pub fn addr(&self) -> std::net::SocketAddr {\n        self.addr\n    }\n\n    pub fn port(&self) -> u16 {\n        self.addr.port()\n    }\n\n    pub fn shutdown(&self) {\n        self.stop\n            .store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for ServerHandle {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        self.shutdown();\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Connection handling\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nstruct Request {\n    method: String,\n    path: String, // path portion only\n    query: String,\n    body: String,\n}\n\nfn handle_connection(mut stream: TcpStream, state: Arc<AppState>) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)))?;\n    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)))?;\n\n    // Read until end of headers, accumulating up to 1 MiB.\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(2048);\n    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];\n    let mut header_end = None;\n    while header_end.is_none() && buf.len() < 1024 * 1024 {\n        match stream.read(&mut byte) {\n            Ok(0) => break,\n            Ok(_) => {\n                buf.push(byte[0]);\n                if buf.len() >= 4 && &buf[buf.len() - 4..] == b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\" {\n                    header_end = Some(buf.len());\n                } else if buf.len() >= 2 && &buf[buf.len() - 2..] == b\"\\n\\n\" {\n                    header_end = Some(buf.len());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => break,\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n    let header_end = match header_end {\n        Some(n) => n,\n        None => {\n            return send_simple(&mut stream, 400, \"malformed request (no header end)\");\n        }\n    };\n\n    let header_text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..header_end]).to_string();\n    let mut lines = header_text.split(\"\\r\\n\").filter(|l| !l.is_empty());\n    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let mut parts = request_line.split_whitespace();\n    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n    let target = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let (path, query) = match target.split_once('?') {\n        Some((p, q)) => (p.to_string(), q.to_string()),\n        None => (target.to_string(), String::new()),\n    };\n    let content_length: usize = header_text\n        .lines()\n        .find_map(|line| {\n            let lower = line.to_ascii_lowercase();\n            lower\n                .strip_prefix(\"content-length:\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse().ok())\n        })\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n\n    let mut body = String::new();\n    if content_length > 0 {\n        // Remaining bytes after the header terminator.\n        let already = buf.len() - header_end;\n        let mut rest = vec![0u8; content_length.saturating_sub(already)];\n        stream.read_exact(&mut rest)?;\n        let mut all = buf[header_end..].to_vec();\n        all.extend_from_slice(&rest);\n        all.truncate(content_length);\n        body = String::from_utf8_lossy(&all).to_string();\n    }\n\n    let req = Request {\n        method,\n        path,\n        query,\n        body,\n    };\n    let (status, json) = route(&req, &state);\n    send_response(&mut stream, status, &json)\n}\n\nfn send_simple(stream: &mut TcpStream, status: u16, msg: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let body = format!(\n        \"{{\\\"ok\\\":{},\\\"error\\\":{}}}\",\n        status == 200,\n        json_string(msg)\n    );\n    send_response(stream, status, &body)\n}\n\nfn send_response(stream: &mut Found\",\n        409 => \"Conflict\",\n        500 => \"Internal Server Error\",\n        _ => \"OK\",\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Ok((status, body)) => (status, body),\n        Err((status, msg)) => (\n            status,\n            format!(\"{{\\\"ok\\\":false,\\\"error\\\":{}}}\", json_string(&msg)),\n        ),\n    }\n}\n\ntype RouteResult = Result<(u16, String), (u16, String)>;\n\nfn err(status: u16, msg: impl Into<String>) -> RouteResult {\n    Err((status, msg.into()))\n}\n\nfn try_route(req: &Request, state: &AppState) -> RouteResult {\n    let path = req.path.trim_end_matches('/');\n\n    if path == \"/health\" && req.method == \"GET\" {\n        return Ok((\n            200,\n            format!(\n    .unwrap_or(0)\n            ),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    if path == \"/series\" && req.method == \"GET\" {\n        let names = state.store.list_series();\n        let arr = names\n \"/dev/fault\" && req.method == \"POST\" {\n        let rules = state\n            .fault_rules\n            .as_ref()\n            .ok_or_else(|| (404, \"fault injection disabled (start server with --fault)\".to_string()))?;\n        for line in req.body.lines().map(str::trim).filter(|l| !l.is_empty()) {\n            if line == \"clear\" {\n                rules.clear();\n            } else if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix(\"write_limit=\") {\n                if v == \"none\" {\n                    rules.clear();\n                } else {\n                    let limit: u64 = parse_i64(v)\n                        .and_then(|x| u64::try_from(x).ok())\n                        .map_err(|_| (400, format!(\"bad write_limit: {v}\")))?;\n                    rules.fail_writes_after(limit);\n                }\n            } else if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix(\"fail_syncs=\") {\n                let n: usize = v\n                    .parse()\n                    .map_err(|_| (400, format!(\"bad fail_syncs: {v}\")))?;\n                rules.fail_next_syncs(n);\n            } else {\n                return err(400, format!(\"unknown fault directive: {line}\"));\n            }\n        }\n        return Ok((\n            200,\n            format!(\n                \"{{\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"bytes_written\\\":{}}}\",\n                rules.bytes_written()\n            ),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // Series-scoped routes.\n    if let Some(rest) = path.strip_prefix(\"/series/\") {\n        let segments: Vec<&str> = rest.split('/').collect();\n        return match segments.as_slice() {\n            [name] if req.method == \"POST\" => create_series(state, name, &req.query),\n            [name, \"stats\"] if req.method == \"GET\" => series_stats(state, name),\n            [name, \"points\"] if req.method == \"POST\" => write_points(state, name, &req.query, &req.body),\n            [name, \"range\"] if req.method == \"GET\" => range_query(state, name, &req.query),\n            [name, \"flush\"] if req.method == \"POST\" => flush_series(state, name),\n            [name, \"drain\"] if req.method == \"POST\" => drain_series(state, name),\n            [name, \"buffered\"] if req.method == \"GET\" => buffered_count(state, name),\n            _ => err(404, format!(\"no such route: {} {}\", req.method, req.path)),\n        };\n    }\n\n    err(404, format!(\"no such route: {} {}\", req.method, req.path))\n}\n\nfn create_series(state: &AppState, name: &str, query: &str) -> RouteResult {\n    let params = parse_query(query);\n    let policy = match params.get(\"policy\").copied().unwrap_or(\"reject\") {\n        \"reject\" => UnorderedPolicy::Reject,\n        \"buffer\" => UnorderedPolicy::Buffer,\n        other => return err(400, format!(\"unknown policy: {other}\")),\n    };\n    let block_size = match params.get(\"block_size\") {\n        Some(v) => Some(\n .create_series(name, policy, block_size)\n        .map_err(store_err_status)?;\n    Ok((\n        201,\n        format!(\n            \"{{\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"series\\\":{},\\\"policy\\\":\\\"{}\\\"}}\",\n            json_string(name),\n            if matches!(policy, UnorderedPolicy::Buffer) {\n                \"buffer\"\n            } else {\n                \"reject\"\n            }\n        ),\n    ))\n}\n\nfn series_stats(state: &AppState, name: &str) -> RouteResult {\n    let s = \"{{\\\"series\\\":{},\\\"policy\\\":\\\"{}\\\",\\\"block_size\\\":{},\\\"blocks\\\":{},\\\"flushed_points\\\":{},\\\"active_points\\\":{},\\\"buffered_points\\\":{},\\\"disk_bytes\\\":{},\\\"uncompressed_bytes\\\":{},\\\"compression_ratio\\\":{}}}\",\n            json_string(name),\n            if matches!(s.policy, UnorderedPolicy::Buffer) { \"buffer\" } else { \"reject\" },\n            s.block_size,\n            s.blocks,\n        match args[i].as_str() {\n            \"--data-dir\" | \"-d\" => {\n                i += 1;\n                data_dir = PathBuf::from(args.get(i).unwrap_or_else(|| usage_and_exit()));\n            }\n            \"--addr\" | \"-a\" => {\n                i += 1;\n                addr = args.get(i).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| usage_and_exit());\n            }\n            \"--block-size\" | other => {\n                eprintln!(\"unknown argument: {other}\");\n                usage_and_exit();\n            }\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    let mode = if fault {\n        FaultMode::On\n    } else {\n        FaultMode::Off\n    };\n\n    let handle = match server::serve(&addr, data_dir.clone(), block_size.max(1), mode) {\n        Ok(h) => h,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"failed to bind {addr}: {e}\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n    };\n\n    println!(\n        \"tsblock listening on http://{} (data_dir={}, block_size={}, fault_injection={})\",\n        handle.addr(),\n        data_dir.display(),\n        block_size,\n        fault\n    );\n\n    let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));\n    let stop_signal = Arc::clone(&stop);\n    ctrlc_setup(stop_signal);\n\n    while !stop.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {\n        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));\n    }\n    handle.shutdown();\n    println!(\"shutting down\");\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(windows))]\nfn ctrlc_setup(stop: Arc<AtomicBool>) {\n    // Best-effort SIGTERM/SIGINT handling without external crates.\n    unsafe {\n        extern wait::requested()\n}\n\n// Minimal libc FFI shim (no dependency crate).\n#[cfg(not(windows))]\nmod libcish {\n    pub type c_int = i32;\n    pub const SIGINT: c_int = 2;\n    pub const SIGTERM: c_int = 15;\n\n    unsafe extern \"C\" {\n        fn signal(signum: c_int, handler: usize) -> usize;\n    }\n\n    pub unsafe fn signal(signum: c_int, handler: usize) -> usize {\n        unsafe { signal(signum, handler) }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(windows)]\nfn ctrlc_setup(_stop: Arc<AtomicBool>) {}\n\nfn print_help() {\n    println!(\n        \"tsblock — file-backed integer time-series block Already-merged\n    /// points stay merged; the rest stay buffered.\n    pub fn drain(&self, name: &str) -> Result<DrainOutcome, StoreError> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g\n            .series\n            .get_mut(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(name.to_string()))?;\n\n        s.late_buffer.sort_by(|a, b| a.ts.cmp(&b.ts)); Already-merged\n    /// points stay merged; the rest stay buffered.\n    pub fn drain(&self, name: &str) -> Result<DrainOutcome, StoreError> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let s = g\n            .series\n            .get_mut(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::UnknownSeries(name.to_string()))?;\n\n        s.late_buffer.sort_by(|a, b| a.ts.cmp(&b.ts)); }","new_string":"    #[test]\n    fn drain_rewrites_history_including_flushed_blocks() {\n        // Even points older than the start of the first flushed block must\n        // land in history: drain compacts and rewrites the whole file.\n        let dir = tempdir(\"drain\");\n        let store = open_store(&dir, 2); // tiny blocks force flushing\n        store.create_series(\"s\", UnorderedPolicy::Buffer, None).unwrap();\n        store\n            .write(\n                \"s\",\n                &[\n                    Point::new(100, 1),\n                    Point::new(200, 2),\n                    Point::new(300, 3),\n                    Point::new(400, 4),\n                ],\n            )\n            .unwrap();\n        store.flush(Some(\"s\")).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(store.stats(\"s\").unwrap().blocks, 2);\n\n        // 50 and 60 predate the first block (ts=100); 250 lands in between.\n        let out = store\n            .write(\"s\", &[Point::new(50, 0), Point::new(250, 9), Point::new(60, 7)])\n            .unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(out.accepted, 0);\n        assert_eq!(out.buffered, 3);\n\n        let d = store.drain(\"s\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(d.merged, 3);\n        assert_eq!(d.buffered_remaining, 0);\n\n        let q = store.query(\"s\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(\n            q.points,\n            vec![\n                Point::new(50, 0),\n                Point::new(60, 7),\n                Point::new(100, 1),\n                Point::new(200, 2),\n                Point::new(250, 9),\n                Point::new(300, 3),\n                Point::new(400, 4),\n            ]\n        );\n        // 7 points at block size 2 -> ceil = 4 rewritten blocks.\n        assert_eq!(store.stats(\"s\").unwrap().blocks, 4);\n        drop(store);\n\n        // The rewrite must survive reopen via the normal recovery scan.\n        let store2 = open_store(&dir, 2);\n        let rep = store2.recovery_report();\n        assert_eq!(rep.torn_records, 0);\n        assert_eq!(rep.blocks_loaded, 4);\n        let q = store2.query(\"s\", 40, 260).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(\n            q.points,\n            vec![\n                Point::new(50, 0),\n                Point::new(60, 7),\n                Point::new(100, 1),\n                Point::new(200, 2),\n                Point::new(250, 9),\n            ]\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn drain_with_empty_buffer_is_noop() {\n        let dir = tempdir(\"drainnoop\");\n        let store = open_store(&dir, Acceptance + failure-injection tests for the storage engine.\n//!\n//! These tests use the injectable I/O layer to simulate ENOSPC / EIO and\n//! verify the documented sync boundary: a torn trailing record is detected\n//! by its CRC and truncated on reopen, while all fully synced records survive.\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse tsblock::coding::Point;\nuse tsblock::io_layer::{FaultRules, FaultyIo, RealIo, EIO, ENOSPC};\nuse tsblock::store::{Store, UnorderedPolicy};\n\nfn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    let d = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"tsblock-it-{tag}-{}-{}\",\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();\n    d\n}\n\nfn make_points(n: i64) -> Vec<Point> {\n    // Timestamps every 60 s, values following a gentle integer walk with\n    // occasional sign changes: exercises DOD, first-difference and zigzag.\n    (0..n)\n        .map(|i| Point::new(1_700_000_000 + i * 60, (i % 13) - 6))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn enospc_mid_record_leaves_truncatable_tail_and_loses_nothing_synced() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"enospc\");\n    let rules = Arc::new(FaultRules::new());\n    let io = Arc::new(FaultyIo::new(Arc::new(RealIo::new()), Arc::clone(&rules)));\n\n    // Phase 1: write two full, synced blocks before any fault is armed.\n    let store = Store::open(&dir, Arc::clone(&io) as Arc<dyn _>, 50).unwrap();\n    store\n        .create_series(\"cpu\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, Some(50))\n        .unwrap();\n    let first100 = make_points(100);\n    let out = store.write(\"cpu\", &first100).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(out.blocks_flushed, 2);\n    drop(store);\n\n    // Phase 2: arm a write budget that fails partway through the next record.\n    let rules2 = Arc::new(FaultRules::new());\n    let io2 = Arc::new(FaultyIo::new(Arc::new(RealIo::new()), Arc::clone(&rules2)));\n    let store2 = Store::open(&dir, io2, 50).unwrap();\n    // Allow only 20 bytes of the next record (record header is 8 bytes), so\n    // the write is genuinely partial.\n    rules2.fail_writes_after(20);\n    let next = make_points(150)[100..150].to_vec();\n    let err = store2.write(\"cpu\", &next).unwrap_err();\n    let raw = err.to_string();\n    assert!(\n        raw.contains(&ENOSPC.to_string()) || raw.contains(\"os error 28\"),\n        \"expected ENOSPC, got {raw}\"\n    );\n\n    // The failed points remain in the active block and can be retried after\n    // the fault is cleared: durability is not silently claimed.\n    rules2.clear();\n    let out = store2.flush(Some(\"cpu\")).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(out, 1);\n    drop(store2);\n\n    // Phase 3: reopen with a pristine backend; recovery must report no torn\n    // record (the successful retry overwrote the torn region positionally).\n    let store3 = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 50).unwrap();\n    let rep = store3.recovery_report();\n    assert_eq!(rep.torn_records, 0, \"{rep:?}\");\n    assert_eq!(rep.blocks_loaded, 3);\n    let all = store3\n        .query(\"cpu\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX)\n        .unwrap()\n        .points;\n    assert_eq!(all.len(), 150);\n    assert_eq!(all, make_points(150));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn torn_record_without_retry_is_truncated_on_reopen() {\n    // Reproduce a crash after a partial write with no retry: directly truncate\n    // the backing file mid-record, then reopen and check recovery truncation.\n    let dir = tempdir(\"torn\");\n    let store = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 40).unwrap();\n    store.create_series(\"m\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, Some(40)).unwrap();\n    let pts = make_points(80);\n    store.write(\"m\", &pts).unwrap(); // 2 synced blocks\n    drop(store);\n\n    let path = dir.join(\"m.tsb\");\n    let len = std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len();\n    // Append a bogus record header and a few garbage payload bytes.\n    {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        let mut f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).open(&path).unwrap();\n        f.write_all(&500u32.to_le_bytes()).unwrap(); // claims 500 bytes\n        f.write_all(&0xDEAD_BEEFu32.to_le_bytes()).unwrap();\n        f.write_all(&[0xAB; 10]).unwrap();\n    }\n    assert_eq!(std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len(), len + 18);\n\n    let store2 = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 40).unwrap();\n    let rep = store2.recovery_report();\n    assert_eq!(rep.series_loaded, 1);\n    assert_eq!(rep.blocks_loaded, 2);\n    assert_eq!(rep.torn_records, 1);\n    // File truncated back to the last valid record boundary.\n    assert_eq!(std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len(), len);\n    let all = store2.query(\"m\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX).unwrap().points;\n    assert_eq!(all, pts);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn failed_fsync_is_surfaced_and_points_remain_retryable() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"eio\");\n    let rules = Arc::new(FaultRules::new());\n    let io = Arc::new(FaultyIo::new(Arc::new(RealIo::new()), Arc::clone(&rules)));\n    let store = Store::open(&dir, io, 10).unwrap();\n    store.create_series(\"s\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, Some(10)).unwrap();\n\n    // First block's write succeeds but its fsync fails with EIO.\n    rules.fail_next_syncs(1);\n    let err = store.write(\"s\", &make_points(10)).unwrap_err();\n    assert!(\n        err.to_string().contains(&EIO.to_string()) || err.to_string().contains(\"os error 5\"),\n        \"expected EIO, got {}\",\n        err\n    );\n\n    // Points are still active; after clearing the fault, flush persists them.\n    rules.clear();\n    assert_eq!(store.flush(Some(\"s\")).unwrap(), 1);\n    let q = store.query(\"s\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(q.points.len(), 10);\n\n    // Reopen: even if the kernel had not kept the bytes, recovery never sees\n    // more than one well-formed record here.\n    drop(store);\n    let store2 = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 10).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(\n        store2.query(\"s\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX).unwrap().points.len(),\n        10\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn extreme_and_duplicate_values_compress_and_roundtrip() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"extreme\");\n    let store = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 1000).unwrap();\n    store.create_series(\"x\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, Some(1000)).unwrap();\n    let pts = vec![\n        Point::new(i64::MIN, i64::MIN),\n        Point::new(i64::MIN, 0),                 // duplicate ts\n        Point::new(i64::MIN + 1, i64::MAX),\n        Point::new(0, -1),\n        Point::new(i64::MAX - 1, i64::MIN),\n        Point::new(i64::MAX, i64::MAX),\n    ];\n    store.write(\"x\", &pts).unwrap();\n    store.flush(Some(\"x\")).unwrap();\n    let got = store.query(\"x\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(got.points, Acceptance + failure-injection tests for the storage engine.\n//!\n//! These tests use the injectable I/O layer to simulate ENOSPC / EIO and\n//! verify the documented sync boundary: a torn trailing record is detected\n//! by its CRC and truncated on reopen, while all fully synced records survive.\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse tsblock::coding::Point;\nuse tsblock::io_layer::{FaultRules, FaultyIo, RealIo, EIO, ENOSPC};\nuse tsblock::store::{Store, UnorderedPolicy};\n\nfn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    let d = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"tsblock-it-{tag}-{}-{}\",\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();\n    d\n}\n\nfn make_points(n: i64) -> Vec<Point> {\n    // Timestamps every 60 s, values following a gentle integer walk with\n    // occasional sign changes: exercises DOD, first-difference and zigzag.\n    (0..n)\n        .map(|i| Point::new(1_700_000_000 + i * 60, (i % 13) - 6))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn enospc_mid_record_leaves_truncatable_tail_and_loses_nothing_synced() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"enospc\");\n    let rules = Arc::new(FaultRules::new());\n    let io = Arc::new(FaultyIo::new(Arc::new(RealIo::new()), Arc::clone(&rules)));\n\n    // Phase 1: write two full, synced blocks before any fault is armed.\n    let store = Store::open(&dir, Arc::clone(&io) as Arc<dyn _>, 50).unwrap();\n    store\n        .create_series(\"cpu\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, Some(50))\n        .unwrap();\n    let first100 = make_points(100);\n    let out = store.write(\"cpu\", &first100).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(out.blocks_flushed, 2);\n    drop(store);\n\n    // Phase 2: arm a write budget that fails partway through the next record.\n    let rules2 = Arc::new(FaultRules::new());\n    let io2 = Arc::new(FaultyIo::new(Arc::new(RealIo::new()), Arc::clone(&rules2)));\n    let store2 = Store::open(&dir, io2, 50).unwrap();\n    // Allow only 20 bytes of the next record (record header is 8 bytes), so\n    // the write is genuinely partial.\n    rules2.fail_writes_after(20);\n    let next = make_points(150)[100..150].to_vec();\n    let err = store2.write(\"cpu\", &next).unwrap_err();\n    let raw = err.to_string();\n    assert!(\n        raw.contains(&ENOSPC.to_string()) || raw.contains(\"os error 28\"),\n        \"expected ENOSPC, got {raw}\"\n    );\n\n    // The failed points remain in the active block and can be retried after\n    // the fault is cleared: durability is not silently claimed.\n    rules2.clear();\n    let out = store2.flush(Some(\"cpu\")).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(out, 1);\n    drop(store2);\n\n    // Phase 3: reopen with a pristine backend; recovery must report no torn\n    // record (the successful retry overwrote the torn region positionally).\n    let store3 = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 50).unwrap();\n    let rep = store3.recovery_report();\n    assert_eq!(rep.torn_records, 0, \"{rep:?}\");\n    assert_eq!(rep.blocks_loaded, 3);\n    let all = store3\n        .query(\"cpu\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX)\n        .unwrap()\n        .points;\n    assert_eq!(all.len(), 150);\n    assert_eq!(all, make_points(150));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn torn_record_without_retry_is_truncated_on_reopen() {\n    // Reproduce a crash after a partial write with no retry: directly truncate\n    // the backing file mid-record, then reopen and check recovery truncation.\n    let dir = tempdir(\"torn\");\n    let store = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 40).unwrap();\n    store.create_series(\"m\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, Some(40)).unwrap();\n    let pts = make_points(80);\n    store.write(\"m\", &pts).unwrap(); // 2 synced blocks\n    drop(store);\n\n    let path = dir.join(\"m.tsb\");\n    let len = std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len();\n    // Append a bogus record header and a few garbage payload bytes.\n    {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        let mut f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).open(&path).unwrap();\n        f.write_all(&500u32.to_le_bytes()).unwrap(); // claims 500 bytes\n        f.write_all(&0xDEAD_BEEFu32.to_le_bytes()).unwrap();\n        f.write_all(&[0xAB; 10]).unwrap();\n    }\n    assert_eq!(std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len(), len + 18);\n\n    let store2 = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 40).unwrap();\n    let rep = store2.recovery_report();\n    assert_eq!(rep.series_loaded, 1);\n    assert_eq!(rep.blocks_loaded, 2);\n    assert_eq!(rep.torn_records, 1);\n    // File truncated back to the last valid record boundary.\n    assert_eq!(std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len(), len);\n    let all = store2.query(\"m\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX).unwrap().points;\n    assert_eq!(all, pts);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn failed_fsync_is_surfaced_and_points_remain_retryable() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"eio\");\n    let rules = Arc::new(FaultRules::new());\n    let io = Arc::new(FaultyIo::new(Arc::new(RealIo::new()), Arc::clone(&rules)));\n    let store = Store::open(&dir, io, 10).unwrap();\n    store.create_series(\"s\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, Some(10)).unwrap();\n\n    // First block's write succeeds but its fsync fails with EIO.\n    rules.fail_next_syncs(1);\n    let err = store.write(\"s\", &make_points(10)).unwrap_err();\n    assert!(\n        err.to_string().contains(&EIO.to_string()) || err.to_string().contains(\"os error 5\"),\n        \"expected EIO, got {}\",\n        err\n    );\n\n    // Points are still active; after clearing the fault, flush persists them.\n    rules.clear();\n    assert_eq!(store.flush(Some(\"s\")).unwrap(), 1);\n    let q = store.query(\"s\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(q.points.len(), 10);\n\n    // Reopen: even if the kernel had not kept the bytes, recovery never sees\n    // more than one well-formed record here.\n    drop(store);\n    let store2 = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 10).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(\n        store2.query(\"s\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX).unwrap().points.len(),\n        10\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn extreme_and_duplicate_values_compress_and_roundtrip() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"extreme\");\n    let store = Store::open(&dir, Arc::new(RealIo::new()), 1000).unwrap();\n    store.create_series(\"x\", UnorderedPolicy::Reject, Some(1000)).unwrap();\n    let pts = vec![\n        Point::new(i64::MIN, i64::MIN),\n        Point::new(i64::MIN, 0),                 // duplicate ts\n        Point::new(i64::MIN + 1, i64::MAX),\n        Point::new(0, -1),\n        Point::new(i64::MAX - 1, i64::MIN),\n        Point::new(i64::MAX, i64::MAX),\n    ];\n    store.write(\"x\", &pts).unwrap();\n    store.flush(Some(\"x\")).unwrap();\n    let got = store.query(\"x\", i64::MIN, i64::MAX).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(got.points, pts);\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"af15e8c3-0af8-441f-8531-04f3fa57c1b5","session_id":"7340a70f-2c1f-48a0-9a1a-9adde575dea4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp7/b","sessionId":"7340a70f-2c1f-48a0-9a1a-9adde575dea4","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp7-b","slug":"refactored-marinating-thompson"}

claims 500 bytes\n        f.write_all(&0xDEAD_BEEFu32.to_le_bytes()).unwrap();\n        f.write_all(&[0xAB; 10]).unwrap();\n    }\n    assert_eq!(std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len(), len + {"parentUuid":"96713e14-d369-475f-80cc-bf58175a6e9e","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_0qq03zx1e7fmx7g92q8lh22y","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp7/b/tests/http_acceptance.rs","content":"//! End-to-end acceptance checks through the real HTTP surface.\n//!\n//! The reference oracle is a plain uncompressed `Vec<(i64, i64)>` built\n//! alongside the writes: every range response must equal the naive\n//! `retain` filter over that array.\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\n\nuse tsblock::server::{self, get, post, FaultMode};\nuse tsblock::coding::Point;\n\nfn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    let d = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"tsblock-http-{tag}-{}-{}\",\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();\n    d\n}\n\n/// Deterministic xorshift64* so the dataset is reproducible.\nstruct Rng(u64);\nimpl Rng {\n    fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {\n        let mut x = self.0;\n        x ^= x >> 12;\n        x ^= x << 25;\n        x ^= x >> 27;\n        self.0 = x;\n        x.wrapping_mul(0x2545_F491_4F6C_DD1D)\n    }\n    fn range(&mut self, n: u64) -> i64 {\n        (self.next() % n) as i64\n    }\n}\n\nfn body_of(points: &[Point]) -> String {\n    points\n        .iter()\n        .map(|p| format!(\"{},{}\", p.ts, p.value))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\"\\n\")\n}\n\n/// Parse `\"points\":[[i,i],[i,i]]` out of a response body.\nfn parse_points(body: &str) -> Vec<Point> {\n    let key = \"\\\"points\\\":[\";\n    let start = body.find(key).unwrap() + key.len();\n    let end = body[start..].find(']').unwrap() + start;\n    let inner = &body[start..end];\n    inner\n        .split(\"],[\")\n        .map(|pair| {\n            let cleaned: String = pair\n                .chars()\n                .filter(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || *c == ',' || *c == '-')\n                .collect();\n            let (ts, v) = cleaned.split_once(',').unwrap();\n            Point::new(ts.parse().unwrap(), v.parse().unwrap())\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\nfn json_u64(body: &str, key: &str) -> u64 {\n    let pat = format!(\"\\\"{key}\\\":\");\n    let i = body.find(&pat).unwrap() + pat.len();\n    let rest = &body[i..];\n    let end = rest\n        .find(|c: char| !(c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '-' || c == '.'))\n        .unwrap_or(rest.len());\n    rest[..end].split('.').next().unwrap().parse().unwrap()\n}\n\nfn json_f64(body: &str, key: &str) -> f64 {\n    let pat = format!(\"\\\"{key}\\\":\");\n    let i = body.find(&pat).unwrap() + pat.len();\n    let rest = &body[i..];\n    let end = rest\n        .find(|c: char| !(c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '-' || c == '.'))\n        .unwrap_or(rest.len());\n    rest[..end].parse().unwrap()\n}\n\nfn reference_filter(points: &[Point], start: i64, end: i64) -> Vec<Point> {\n    points\n        .iter()\n        .copied()\n        .filter(|p| p.ts >= start && p.ts <= end)\n        .collect()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn full_acceptance_over_http() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"accept\");\n    let handle = server::serve(\n        \"127.0.0.1:0\",\n        dir,\n        100,\n        FaultMode::On, // enables /dev/fault\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    let addr = handle.addr();\n\n    // ---- build the reference dataset and write it ----------------------\n    let mut rng = Rng(0x1234_5678_9ABC_DEF0);\n    let n = 5000usize;\n    let mut reference = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n    let mut ts = 1_700_000_000i64;\n    let mut value = -50i64;\n    for i in 0..n {\n        let .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\"\\n\")\n}\n\n/// Parse `\"points\":[[i,i],[i,i]]` out of a response body.\nfn parse_points(body: &str) -> Vec<Point> {\n    let key = \"\\\"points\\\":[\";\n {\n            let cleaned: String = pair\n                .chars()\n                .filter(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || *c == ',' || *c == '-')\n                .collect();\n            let (ts, v) = cleaned.split_once(',').unwrap();\n            Point::new(ts.parse().unwrap(), v.parse().unwrap())\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\nfn json_u64(body: &str, key: &str) -> u64 {\n    let pat =
